title: Every automated test record gets an outcome, and one that did not run is failed with did not run
when: With a fixture repository whose spec has three automated test records and one that is not automated yet, and suites' output in which two of the automated tests ran: assure record runs at the commit checked out.
then: It exits 0, and the predicate holds one outcome for each automated test record, in ID order. The test that did not run is failed with the detail did not run. The record that is not automated yet has no outcome.

title: The suites job fails for a missing, extra, cut or incomplete part, and for a failed test or package of any name
when: The test runs the join step and the failure check of the proof run workflow's suites job with bash and pipefail on artifact folders of the five parts: a whole set, and sets with a missing part, an extra part, a cut JSON line, a listed package with no result, a root package in no part, no Python output, a failed Go test whose name has no ID, a failed package, and a failed Python test whose name has no ID. It also reads how the tests job splits cmd/stego.
then: The whole set joins and passes. Each set with a missing, extra, cut or incomplete part fails the join, so no proof run is recorded or attested. Each set with a failed test or package, of any name, joins and then fails the suites job. The stego-build part selects cmd/stego's tests with go test -run and the stego part leaves them out with go test -skip, by the same pattern, so each test runs in exactly one part.

title: Outcomes come from Go and Python subtests by the ID in their names, and a test with no ID is ignored
when: The Python runner runs a suite with a passing subtest that carries an ID and a failing subtest that carries none. The go test -json output has a passing and a failing subtest with IDs, and a failing subtest with no ID. assure record reads both.
then: The outcome of each automated test record is that of the subtest that carries its ID: passed, failed and passed. The failing tests with no ID give no outcome and do not refuse the run.

title: An outcome for an ID that is not a test record refuses the run, and no predicate is written
when: assure record reads go test -json output with a subtest that carries an ID that is not a test record in the spec at the commit.
then: It exits non-zero, names the ID, and writes no predicate and no step output.

title: The subject is the full commit checked out, and a short ID, a branch or another commit is refused
when: With a fixture repository at its second commit: assure record runs with a short ID, with the name of the branch checked out, with the first commit, and then with the full commit checked out. The attest job's subject step of proof-run.yml runs for that commit.
then: The first three runs exit non-zero and write nothing. The last writes a predicate about the commit checked out, and the subject step names that commit as the subject, with the SHA-256 of its ID as the digest.

title: A tree with uncommitted changes is refused, also when git status hides them
when: assure record runs in fixture repositories with a changed file, a staged change, an untracked file, a change hidden by skip-worktree, an automated test record added to the spec and hidden by assume-unchanged, an untracked file hidden by info/exclude, an untracked file hidden by the user's excludes file, another commit's tree shown by a replace ref, a same-size change hidden by minimal stat checks, and a new file hidden by an untracked .gitignore that ignores itself. Each hidden case first shows that git status shows no change.
then: Each run exits non-zero, says that the tree has uncommitted changes, and writes nothing.

title: Only the trusted workflow's attestation job signs the proof run, it runs no repository code, and CI commits no evidence file
when: Reads the proof-run.yml workflow, and reads it key by key: the workflow, and the attest job with every key and every step with each of its keys and values, in order, against the keys, steps and values allowed. Runs its subject step with a branch name, and its predicate check step with a predicate about the commit and with one about another commit. Then assure record runs as a job of another workflow, and then with a predicate file in the repository.
then: The workflow and its suites job may only read the repository, and the workflow has only its allowed keys and no environment but the commit and the Lathe pin. Of the jobs that sign a proof run, only the attest job may write an identity token and attestations. The attest job is exactly: needs the suites job, may only get an identity token and write attestations, has no condition, container or defaults, and its four steps: download the proof run, check that it is about the commit, name the commit as the subject, and sign it with actions/attest at the proof run predicate type with the subject that the subject step names; it checks out and runs no code of the repository. Every action is pinned to a commit, and no step commits or pushes. The suites job checks out the pull request head or the commit pushed and records the proof run at it, under the runner's temporary folder, with assure built in the base checkout's cmd/assure, which is the pull request's base commit or the commit pushed, with workspace mode off, into a folder under the runner's temporary folder that the build step makes read-only, before any step runs code of the change, and after a Go setup that restores no cache. The subject step refuses a branch, and the predicate check refuses a predicate about another commit. Both runs of assure record exit non-zero, write nothing, and leave the repository with no change.

title: A change under which an obligation falls is refused, and one that only adds unbuilt, unproved obligations passes
when: With a fixture repository whose base head has two invariants built and proved, one only designed and a constraint only designed: assure gate change runs for a change that adds an invariant with no rule and no test, and then for a change that adds it and also removes the rules' file and one test record, each with a passed proof run at its commit.
then: The first change passes with no reason, and the decision gives its coverage. The second exits non-zero and names each obligation that fell with its share: both invariants from built, and one also from proved.

title: A change is not gated when Lathe finds an error in the spec at the base head or at the change
when: assure gate change runs, with a passed proof run, for a change that drops every rule, test record and rules file against a base head whose spec has a dangling test record, and then for a change with that dangling test record against a clean base head.
then: Each run exits 2, prints no decision, and names the error Lathe finds, so a spec with errors is never read as an empty coverage.

title: A change that retires an obligation to a successor with each standing it had at the base passes, and the decision reports the retirement
when: With a fixture repository whose base head has two invariants built and proved, one only designed and a constraint only designed: assure gate change runs, with a passed proof run at its commit, for a change that renames a built and proved invariant, with its rule, test record and test, and adds a retirement that names the old invariant with the new one as its successor.
then: The change passes with no reason, and the decision reports the retirement as retirement, its ID, the retired invariant and succeeded by the new invariant.

title: A change whose retirement names a successor without a standing the retired obligation had at the base is refused, and the reason names the retirement
when: With the same fixture repository: assure gate change runs, with a passed proof run at its commit, for a change that renames a built and proved invariant with its rule but removes its test record and test, and adds a retirement that names the old invariant with the new one as its successor.
then: The change exits non-zero with one reason: the old invariant is retired by the retirement, but its successor, the new invariant, is not proved. The decision reports no retirement as followed.

title: A retirement with no successor admits the removal of the obligation it names, and a removal that no retirement names is still refused
when: With the same fixture repository: assure gate change runs, with a passed proof run at its commit, for a change that removes the invariant that is only designed and adds a retirement with no successor that names it; then for a change that also removes the constraint, which no retirement names.
then: The first change passes with no reason, and the decision reports that the retirement's invariant has no successor. The second exits non-zero with one reason, that the constraint is absent at the change and was designed at the base, and the decision still reports the retirement.

title: A change with no verified proof run at its commit, or with an automated test record not passed there, is refused
when: assure gate change runs for one change with a store that keeps no attestation; one forged attestation and one about another commit; a proof run signed at another pull request's ref; a proof run with a failed test and a test with no outcome; one with a skipped test; and one in which every automated test passed.
then: Each run but the last exits non-zero. With no proof run that verifies, the reason says there is no verified proof run at the commit and why each attestation is refused. Otherwise each test record that did not pass is named with its result. The last run passes.

title: A refusal names each obligation that fell with its share and each test record that did not pass, and exits non-zero
when: assure gate change runs, with the job's step summary file set, for a change that removes the rules' file, a test record and an invariant, and whose proof run has the remaining automated test failed. Then it runs, with another step summary file, for a change whose spec has a test record that names a file that does not exist. Then it runs with that summary file set and no --base.
then: It exits non-zero and says the change is refused. The reasons are each on a line of their own: each obligation that fell, with each share it fell from, the invariant the change removes as absent at the change with the share it had at the base, and the failed test record. The step summary holds the same decision, and the repository has no change. For the change with the broken spec it exits 2 and prints no decision, and the other step summary holds one line that says no decision was reached and names Lathe's error. With no --base it exits 2, and the summary holds one line that says no decision was reached because the gate is called wrongly.

title: The same commit, base and proof run give the same decision and reasons in the same order
when: assure gate change runs twice for a change refused for five reasons, with a change-grade proof run and a forged one; then a third time with the store giving the attestations in the other order and with changes in the working tree.
then: The three runs give the same exit code and the same decision, byte for byte.

title: A change is refused for a code-standard fault the base head does not have, and a fault the base has is reported, not refused
when: With a fixture repository whose base head has two code-standard faults, a Go file no record names and a rule record whose identifier its file does not declare, and a passed proof run at each change: assure gate change runs for a change that adds another Go file no record names, for a change that keeps the base's faults, for a change under which the rule record names another identifier its file does not declare, and for a change that removes the unnamed file of the base.
then: The first change exits 1 and names the new file with its rule and key as the one reason; its code faults list all three by rule and key, the new one as not at base and the others as present at base. The second change passes and reports both faults of the base as present at base. The third passes: the fault keeps its rule and key, and is reported with its new reason as present at base. The fourth passes and reports only the fault that remains.

title: A proof run signed at the change's own ref counts only while the workflows folder is the base's, and one signed at main counts for any tree
when: assure gate change runs for a change that alters, adds and removes a workflow file, first with a passed proof run signed at the change's own ref, then with one signed at main; then for a change that leaves the workflows folder as the base has it, with a passed proof run signed at its own ref.
then: The first run is refused: no verified proof run, because the change alters the workflows folder, and each file that differs is named. The second and third runs pass.

title: A proof run signed at the change's own ref by a run at a merge of another commit, or into another branch, is refused
when: In a fixture repository, a pull request's earlier head alters the proof run workflow and its later head leaves the workflows folder as the base has it. assure gate change runs for the later head with a passed proof run signed at the change's own ref by a run at the merge commit of the earlier head; then by a run at the later head itself, which is no merge commit; then by a run at a commit that the provider does not keep; then by a run at the merge commit of the later head into the earlier head, as for a pull request whose base was another branch before it was retargeted; then by a run at the merge commit of the later head. The fixture store gives the parents of each commit as GitHub's git commits API does.
then: The first four runs are refused with exactly one reason: no verified proof run, because the run's commit is not a merge commit whose second parent is the later head, with the parents the provider gives, or, for the fourth, because the merge commit's first parent is not the base head. The last run passes.

title: The gate job builds assure from the base commit only, and runs it in the change's checkout with the pinned Lathe, which the change cannot alter
when: Reads the proof run workflow, its gate job and every key of the job and its steps, and compares the job with the expected job that the test holds. Then, in a fixture repository, assure gate change runs with a Lathe that a run on the change's tree rewrites, so that a run of the rewritten Lathe gives no coverage, for a change that rewrites it and has a passed proof run; then it runs again with the rewritten Lathe.
then: The gate job is exactly the expected job: each key of the job, and each step in order with each of its keys (run, with, env, uses, working-directory, if, shell and any other), so that no text that shell quoting hides can enter it; the workflow runs only on a push to main, a pull request and by hand. In that job: the workflow and the job have no defaults and no key that lets a failed step pass, and the job has no environment of its own; the workflow's environment is only the change's commit and LATHE_REF, a full commit. The job runs on each pull request unless the run is cancelled, may only read the repository, uses only the checkout, setup-go and setup-node actions, and restores no cache. Between the change's checkout and the base's, one step finds the base: the merge commit's first parent, checked to descend from the payload base and lie on the base branch, with a check that the merge commit's second parent is the change's head; it runs only git, in the change's checkout, and gives the base as its output. The job checks out exactly three things: the change's commit with its full history into stego, Lathe at LATHE_REF, and the base that it found into a folder of its own, with no other input, so it never builds the gate from the head, the merge commit, or a base with no checks. Each step sets only the environment it needs, by its exact value: workspace mode off for the build, and the base and the token for the gate. The only go command of the job builds assure in the base's cmd/assure, after that checkout, into the runner's temporary folder. No step but the gate and the step that finds the base runs in or names the change's checkout, runs git, or runs a package manager, an interpreter or a script outside Lathe's folder, and every step before the gate runs. Right before the gate, a step makes Lathe and the built binary read-only. The gate step runs exactly that binary in the change's checkout, for the change's commit against the base that the job found, with one --lathe that names the Lathe built from LATHE_REF, and with only the base and the token in its environment. The first gate run passes, and the change's run did rewrite the Lathe: the base was measured before it. The second run gives no decision, as the rewritten Lathe cannot measure the base.

title: A release is refused while any obligation is not designed, built and proved, and each such obligation is named
when: With a fixture repository and a passed proof run signed at main at each commit: assure gate release runs at a commit whose spec has an obligation Lathe counts as neither built nor proved and one it counts as not proved, and then at a commit whose every obligation is designed, built and proved.
then: The first decision is refused, gives the coverage at the commit, names each obligation with each share it does not have (one not proved, the other not built and not proved), and no decision predicate is written. The fully proved commit passes.
notes: Measures ST-BO07: the share of obligations designed, built and proved is what this gate reads, and a release passes only at 100%.

title: A release commit with no verified proof run, or with an automated test record not passed there, is refused
when: With a fixture repository whose release commit is fully proved: assure gate release runs with a store that keeps no attestation; with a forged attestation; with a proof run signed at main in which a test failed and one has no outcome; with one in which a test was skipped; and with one in which every automated test passed.
then: Each run but the last exits 1 and writes no predicate. With no proof run that verifies, the reason says there is no verified proof run at the commit and why. Otherwise each test record that did not pass is named with its result. The last run passes.

title: The release gate job runs on a push to main, and only the attest-release job, which runs no repository code, signs a passed decision with the commit as subject
when: Reads proof-run.yml key by key: the workflow, and the gate-release and attest-release jobs with every key of each job and every step with each of its keys and values, in order, against the keys, steps and values allowed. Runs the gate-release job's gate step with an assure that exits 0, 1, 2 and 3. Runs the attest-release job's subject step for a commit and for a branch name, and its predicate check step with a passed release decision about the commit, one about another commit, a refused one, one of the change gate and one with no kind.
then: The workflow has only its allowed keys, read-only permissions and no environment but the commit and the Lathe pin. The gate-release job is exactly: needs the attest job, runs on each push to main also when the suites or the attest job fail, may only read the repository, gives the gate step's output passed as its own, and its nine steps: check out the commit with its full history and the pinned Lathe, set up Go with no cache and Node, build Lathe, build assure, remove the Go problem matcher, run assure gate release with the commit, a predicate under the runner's temporary folder and the Lathe the workflow builds, and upload the predicate only when passed is true; no other step has a condition or goes on after an error. The gate step gives passed=true for exit 0, ends green with passed=false for a refused release (exit 1), and fails with no output for exit 2 or 3. Every action is pinned to a commit. Only the attest and attest-release jobs may get an identity token or write attestations. The attest-release job is exactly: needs the gate-release job and runs only when its output passed is true, may only get an identity token and write attestations, has no container or defaults, and its four steps: download the predicate, check it, name the commit as the subject, and sign it with actions/attest at the release-decision predicate type; it checks out and runs no code of the repository. The subject step names the commit as the subject with the SHA-256 of its ID as the digest and refuses the branch, and the check accepts only the passed release decision about the commit.

title: A release commit whose tree has a code-standard fault is refused, and each fault is named with its file and rule
when: With a fixture repository whose release commit is fully proved, and a passed proof run signed at main: assure gate release runs at a commit that adds a Go file no record names and names, in a rule record, an identifier that the rule's file does not declare.
then: It exits 1 and writes no predicate. The decision gives a coverage of 100% for each share, lists both faults in its code faults with the file and the rule, ST-STD-CODE-R02 before ST-STD-CODE-R05, and names each as a reason with its file, the rule and its key.

title: A release takes only a proof run signed at main, and one signed at any other ref is refused with the ref named
when: With a fixture repository whose release commit is fully proved: assure gate release runs with a passed proof run signed at a pull request's ref, then with one signed at another branch, then with both one signed at the pull request's ref and one signed at main.
then: The first two runs exit 1, write no predicate, and say that there is no verified proof run at the commit because the attestation is signed at that ref, not at refs/heads/main. The third run passes, and its decision rests on the proof run signed at main.

title: The ledger comes from verified attestations and the committed spec, and no file of the working tree changes it
when: With a fixture repository of five commits and a store that keeps proof run attestations for four of them, one of which fails verification: assure ledger runs for the newest commit with a clean tree; then with the working tree at the oldest commit, its spec changed and evidence files that say every test passed; then with a store that keeps no attestation; then for a commit with no spec, with a short commit ID, with no commit and with a depth of zero.
then: The first two runs print the same ledger, byte for byte, from the committed spec and the verified attestations, and the repository has no change. With no attestation every result is none, no test record has passed, and it exits 1. The commit with no spec and the wrong calls exit 2 and print no ledger.

title: Each test record shows its state, its result at the commit and the newest commit a verified proof run passed it at, within the depth
when: With a fixture repository of five commits whose newest has a proof run with one automated test failed, the next none, the next one that fails verification and the next both automated tests passed: assure ledger runs for the newest commit twice, then with --depth 2, then for a commit whose proof run passed every test, then with a store in which a test never passed.
then: Each line gives the test record, its state, its result at the commit and the newest commit it passed at; the walk passes over the commit with no attestation, asks for each commit once, and stops where every automated test has passed. The two runs give the same text. With --depth 2 the failed test says not within 2 commits. When every automated test passed it exits 0 and lists only the manual test as not passed; otherwise it exits 1. A test that never passed makes the walk reach the root commit.

title: An attestation that fails verification gives no result at its commit, and the ledger says why
when: With the history of ST-ASR-UC04-R02-T01 and the attestation at the newest commit forged: assure ledger runs for that commit. Then, with change-grade proof runs signed at a pull request's ref: it runs for a change, without and with GITHUB_REF set to that ref; for a commit made as a pull request's merge ref, whose first parent is main's head, with a change-grade attestation, one signed at main by a run at another commit and one signed at a branch at commit 4; for a change that alters a workflow file, also with two statements signed at that ref whose certificates name another source repository and another source ref; and with --base or --main naming the commit itself (the reviewer's spoof).
then: An attestation that is unverifiable or change grade shows as none, with the reason. At the forged commit every result is none, the proof run line says none is verified at release grade, and a line for that commit and one for the forged ancestor give the verifier's reason; the passes come from the older verified proof run, and it exits 1. Each change-grade attestation, at the commit or at an ancestor, is listed as change grade at its ref, counting only in its own gate, and gives no result, with GITHUB_REF set or not; it exits 1. For the merge ref the last passes come from the release-grade proof runs of its first-parent history, and the attestation signed at main by a run at another commit and the one at a branch are refused with their reasons. The two statements whose certificates name another source are refused with that reason, not listed as change grade. --base and --main are not flags of assure ledger: it exits 2 and prints no ledger.

title: A failed resolution leaves go.mod and go.sum as they were
when: With a project that stego apply made and stego deps resolved: a source file imports a module that does not exist, and stego deps runs.
then: stego deps fails; go.mod and go.sum keep their bytes, and no apply journal is left.

title: An interrupted resolution leaves the module files as they were, or as resolved
when: With a project that stego apply made, and the resolved pair of go.mod and go.sum known: the old pair is restored and stego deps runs seven times, each time with an interrupt signal after a longer delay, and stego recover runs when stego deps asks for recovery.
then: At least one run is interrupted; after each run no apply journal is left, and go.mod and go.sum are together either the old pair or the resolved pair.
notes: The interrupt reaches a run at a point that depends on timing. The in-package test ST-BLD-INV01-T interrupts each point of the apply journal by injection.

title: Resolution checks the fills with the go.mod it resolves, once fills exist
when: With the inventory project of the fifth walkthrough (testdata/walkthrough5) from stego init, with the fills of its command, query and consuming worker written, each with a test file, and qualified by stego test and stego fill sign with a key that the test run makes for the test only (ST-EXT-TD02): the first apply runs, go mod download adds the go.sum entry of the runtime's go.mod, as a go build before stego deps asks, then stego validate and stego apply run; a file that imports os is added to a fill and stego deps runs; the file is removed and stego deps runs again.
then: Validate and apply pass and change neither go.mod nor go.sum. The first stego deps fails, names the fill and os, keeps go.mod and go.sum and leaves no apply journal. The second stego deps writes the resolved go.mod, and validate passes after it.
notes: Finding B4 of the fifth walkthrough (2026-11-17): the fill check ran a read-only go list with the project's go.mod before resolution, so stego deps, validate and apply all stopped once go.mod needed an update, and only a manual go mod tidy went on. The check now lists a fill with a completed copy of go.mod and go.sum when the project's go.mod does not hold the modules yet, and stego deps checks the fills with the go.mod and go.sum it resolves, before it writes them.

title: A saved overlay flag and ambient GOFLAGS cannot change what resolution reads
when: With a resolved project, a local module that a saved -overlay flag would import, a Go configuration file that saves that flag and turns the module proxy off, and an invalid ambient GOFLAGS: stego deps runs.
then: The overlay's import never reaches go.mod, and the source is unchanged.

title: Resolution ignores an ambient vendor flag and a missing go.work
when: With a project that stego apply made, a local replace directive, GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor and GOWORK naming a missing file: stego deps runs twice.
then: Both runs succeed, give the same go.mod, and keep the local replacement.

title: Resolution refuses out-of-date generated code and names apply
when: With a project whose code was never applied, and then with a project whose declaration changed after apply: stego deps runs.
then: Each run fails, the error names stego apply, and no project file changes.

title: A downloaded cache holds only the zips whose hashes go.sum states
when: With a committed module that needs one small module, its hash in go.sum, and the pinned Go SDK: stego build download runs.
then: The cache holds exactly one zip, that of the module go.sum states.
notes: It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass.

title: A zip whose hash differs from go.sum stops the download, which names both hashes
when: With a committed module whose go.sum states a wrong hash for its one dependency, and the pinned Go SDK: stego build download runs.
then: The download fails, names the module, its version, the hash go.sum states and the hash of the zip, and leaves nothing in the parent folder.
notes: It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass.

title: The cache record lists each module by path, version and hash, and the revision it serves
when: With a committed module that needs one small module, and the pinned Go SDK: stego build download runs.
then: module-cache.json names the commit and lists the one module with its path, its version and the hash go.sum states. stego build download prints one line that names the revision, the output folder, the count of modules and the record file.
notes: It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass. The printed line is from the walkthrough re-run (2026-11-14), where build download printed nothing; mutation caught (fu-76-mut.py): no line printed.

title: A module the proxy cannot supply stops the download, which names it and leaves nothing
when: With a committed module that needs a module the module proxy cannot supply, and the pinned Go SDK: stego build download runs.
then: The download fails, names that module and its version, and leaves no cache folder, no record and no work folder.
notes: It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass.

title: An interrupted download leaves no cache folder and no record
when: With a committed module that needs one small module, and the pinned Go SDK: stego build download runs six times, each time with an interrupt signal after a longer delay.
then: At least one download is interrupted. Each interrupted download fails and leaves nothing in its parent folder; each complete one leaves the cache folder with its record.
notes: The interrupt reaches a download at a point that depends on timing. It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass.

title: A target that exists or overlaps, or an SDK that is not pinned, is refused by name before any work
when: With a source folder and a fake Go SDK: stego build download runs with a target that exists, a target inside the source, a target inside the SDK, and then with a new target and the fake SDK.
then: Each run is refused and names the target or the SDK, with what it found and what it expected, and no file or folder is made, so no command and no network connection ran.

title: A target with ./ and a file:// source are taken, and a bad flag is refused by its name and value
when: With a source folder and a fake Go SDK: stego build download runs with the target ./cmd/tiny, with the source as a file:// URL, with the target ../cmd/tiny, with the source https://example.com/service.git, and with a file:// URL that names a host.
then: Expects the first two to pass the checks of the flags and be refused only for the SDK that is not pinned; and each of the other three to be refused with the flag, the value found (for a URL, only its scheme and host) and what is expected; and no run to change the folder.
notes: Developer walkthrough of 2026-11-13, step 25 side notes: --target ./out was refused as 'requires a commit, relative module, and relative target', and --source file://... was read as a local path. checkLocation now names each flag; stego build takes the same checks. Mutations caught: no removal of ./ from the target; no file:// source.

title: A refused --source names only the scheme and the host of a URL, so no token is shown
when: stego build download and stego build run with --source set to https, ssh and file URLs that hold user info with a token, one with two @ signs, three with a raw /, ? or # in the user info, one with a token in the path, query and fragment, an scp-style user:TOKEN@host:path that is read as a local path, and two values whose scheme is not one of RFC 3986 and holds a token.
then: Expects each run to be refused with --source and only the scheme and the host of the URL, or only the scheme when the host is not certain, or the cause with no path for the local path; and no part of the user info, path, query or fragment in the refusal.
notes: Security review low S3 of #269, S3 of #273 and the low of #278 (CWE-532). Mutations caught: no @ guard when the parser finds no user info; the path kept; the raw path error in download and in build; the path error not unwrapped; the raw scheme shown.

The two runs against the first are staged and the kept tree is a file only its owner reads; the run against the fork is refused because its tiles do not prove a signed tree; the run with no kept tree is staged. Each bad kept tree is removed with a warning that names the file and the good tree is kept again; the unsafe folder and the linked folder are left out with a warning and hold no tree; the second run waits until the lock is released. title: A create writes the relationship through the outbox after commit, and the stored instance holds the consistency token

notes: The test runs stego apply on the declaration of ST-DECL-TD03 in the form that the runtime data path generates, builds the service with the pinned Go SDK and drives it over HTTP, against PostgreSQL in a local container and the fakes of ST-DECL-TD05 (ST-STD-LOCAL). The fake authorization provider is a SpiceDB gRPC server in the process of the check; it holds the relationships that it gets and records each call. The host test is internal/compiler/relationship_outbox_test.go. On the runtime data path the create of the top-level Todo is public (ST-SUP-RC29-OC01), and a public create cannot write a field-sourced relationship (ST-SUP-Q118), so the owner relationship has the subject source caller. u1 sends owner_id u1. The check reads the Todo and the outbox in one snapshot, and the fake reads whether the row of the Todo is committed when the write comes.

when: From ST-DIS-TD02: stego fleet measures runs on the six checkouts and the registry checkout in a namespace with no network.
then: Expects it to exit 0 and to print each measure that ST-DIS-QRY05 lists for ST-BO01, ST-BO03, ST-BO04 and ST-BO08, with the same figures as a run with the network.
notes: It runs the binary in a network namespace with no interface but loopback (unshare -n, as an unprivileged user), so that any network call fails.

title: A checkout without a readable record counts against every share
when: From ST-DIS-TD02: stego fleet measures runs on the six checkouts, and the test counts each share by hand from the records.
then: Expects each share to have six services as its total, and echo and foxtrot never to count as meeting it. Expects the ST-BO03 share to be the count of services among alpha to delta that meet all four of its conditions, over six.

title: Each measure names the services it is computed from, and they give its figure
when: From ST-DIS-TD02: stego fleet measures runs on the six checkouts with its structured output.
then: Expects each measure to name the services behind it. Expects each figure, computed again by the test from the records of only those services, to equal the figure printed.

title: Publishing starts only from a passed release decision attested at the commit by proof-run.yml at main
when: The publish-release job runs at a commit with no release decision, with a refused decision, with a decision about another commit, with a change decision, with a passed decision that another workflow signed, and with a passed decision of proof-run.yml at main.
then: Each run without the trusted signer's passed decision fails with a line that says nothing is published, reads nothing after the decision, and creates no release; the run with it publishes.
notes: The test runs the job's steps with bash as GitHub Actions does, with a fake gh at the edge that answers from fixed records, and the real jq, unzip and coreutils. It reaches no GitHub service.

title: The release is compiler-<full commit> at the full commit with exactly the four assets, each fetched by artifact ID and verified before upload
when: The publish-release job runs for a passed decision and a successful signed artifact run; then again with an archive whose digest differs from the listed one, two artifacts of one name, an expired artifact, an extra file in an archive, a checksum list that differs, a signature from another run, no signature, another bundle, and a build record of another commit.
then: The first run downloads the two artifacts by their IDs, verifies both signed files against the bundle, and creates compiler-<commit> with the full commit as target and exactly the executable, build.json, SHA256SUMS and provenance.jsonl, with the run and the compiler digest in the notes. Each other run fails with its cause named and creates no release.
notes: The test runs the job's steps with bash as GitHub Actions does, with a fake gh at the edge that answers from fixed records, and the real jq, unzip and coreutils. It reaches no GitHub service.

title: The job takes the newest successful compiler-artifact.yml run on main at the commit from a push or a dispatch, waits for it within a bound, and stops naming the runs when none can succeed
when: The publish-release job runs where the runs at the commit hold the signed run 202 and an older successful run, and newer runs that failed, ran on another branch, ran for a pull request, belong to another workflow or are in progress; then with only a dispatch of main; with a run in progress that succeeds at the second look; with a run in progress at the bound; and with only a failed run, only a pull request run, or only a run on another branch.
then: With the decoys it takes run 202 and names it in the notes; the dispatch publishes; the job waits for the run in progress and publishes; at the bound it fails naming the run; when every run has completed and none can be taken it stops at once naming the runs. No failed run creates a release.
notes: The test runs the job's steps with bash as GitHub Actions does, with a fake gh at the edge that answers from fixed records, and the real jq, unzip and coreutils. It reaches no GitHub service.

title: The release is created not latest and must be immutable; an existing tag or release stops publishing and names the tag
when: The publish-release job runs for a passed decision; then again where the tag exists, where a release of the tag exists, where the repository makes the release mutable, where the release becomes the latest, and where the upload changes an asset.
then: The first run creates the release with --latest=false and publishes it. An existing tag or release fails the job naming the tag, and nothing is created; a mutable release fails the job and tells the owner to enable immutability and delete the release and its tag; a latest release fails the job and tells the owner to mark the previous latest release as latest explicitly, not to delete this release, whose immutable tag can never be used again, and to qualify it by hand with qualify-compiler-release.py --verify-release for the commit; a changed asset fails the job. No failed run gives the release output.
notes: The test runs the job's steps with bash as GitHub Actions does, with a fake gh at the edge that answers from fixed records, and the real jq, unzip and coreutils. It reaches no GitHub service.

title: Each push to main whose gate passed publishes in the same run; a refused decision skips publishing and leaves the run green; no decision fails it
when: Reads proof-run.yml, compiler-artifact.yml and checks.yml, runs the gate step of the gate-release job with assure exiting 0, 1 and 2, and runs the publish-release job for a passed decision.
then: proof-run.yml runs on a push to main; the publish-release job needs gate-release and attest-release and runs only when passed is true; each push has a concurrency group of its own in the three workflows; compiler-artifact.yml builds on every push to main. The gate step gives passed=true for 0, passed=false and a green step for 1, and fails for 2. The publish job publishes.
notes: The test runs the job's steps with bash as GitHub Actions does, with a fake gh at the edge that answers from fixed records, and the real jq, unzip and coreutils. It reaches no GitHub service.

title: The only job that can write releases checks out nothing, runs only shell with gh and jq, and publishes from an empty folder
when: Reads the publish-release job of proof-run.yml and every job's permissions, then runs the job with only gh, jq, unzip and coreutils on the PATH, in an empty working folder.
then: The job has exactly its allowed keys, contents: write and actions: read, and four shell steps with no action, no checkout, no working folder and no interpreter or repository path; no other job can write contents; it takes the commit from COMMIT; it publishes and leaves the working folder empty.
notes: The test runs the job's steps with bash as GitHub Actions does, with a fake gh at the edge that answers from fixed records, and the real jq, unzip and coreutils. It reaches no GitHub service.

title: A passed release creates the tag of the pinned runtime version once, and never moves a tag that exists
when: The publish-release job runs for a passed decision at a commit whose archetypes pin a runtime version with no tag; then again where the tag exists at the same commit and where it exists at another commit; then the job runs for a refused decision.
then: Expects the tag registry/runtime/vX.Y.Z at the release commit after the first run; no change to a tag that exists in the second and the third run; and no tag after a refused decision.
notes: Level: system. Belongs in scripts/test_release_publishing.py beside ST-DIS-UC11-R03-T01, with the fake gh that the other publishing tests use (ST-STD-LOCAL). The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that the release job, not a person, makes the runtime tag.

title: Applying the plan writes platform requirements that state each need of the components, with its keys and ports
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set.
then: Expects the plan to list the platform requirements file, and the file to state each of the nine needs of the components: the secret orders-database with the keys url and password, the configuration value LOG_LEVEL, the backing store orders-db, the topic order-events, the identity issuer sso, the ingress http, the egress destination payments with port 443, the cluster permission and the pod security level restricted, each with the component that needs it. No need is missing.
notes: That the file holds no need that the components do not state is ST-DLV-DS01, which ST-DLV-DS01-T02 proves; this test does not assert it. The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: The shipped components state their real platform needs, and an environment file with no database does not meet them
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set with the shipped registry as it is, and stego env check then runs on an environment file that gives only the three configuration values of the walkthrough file staging-nodb.yaml.
then: Expects the platform requirements to state the secrets orders-database, orders-database-relay, orders-query-cursor and orders-spicedb with their keys, the backing store orders-db, the topic orders-events, the identity issuer orders-issuer, the ingress http on port 8080, the egress destinations orders-db-network, orders-issuer-keys, orders-kafka and spicedb with their ports and the pod security level restricted, no need name to hold a setting value, and the check to fail and name the missing backing store, secret, identity issuer, ingress and egress.
notes: Walkthrough 3, G6, follow-up #331. The other tests of ST-DLV-UC01 clear the needs of the shipped components in their registry copy, so that ST-DLV-TD02 stays the file of the needs of ST-DLV-TD01.

title: A need name or a resource name that is not a Kubernetes name is refused at the requirements stage with a clear message
when: Derives the platform requirements of needs whose name holds a capital letter, '_', a setting value in capital letters or a '-' at the end, and of a cluster permission whose resource name holds them; then of a lower-case secret need and a required variable; then of a component that states the configuration need STEGO_STORE_REGION; then loads platform requirements whose secret requirement is Orders_Database.
then: Expects each need to be refused with the component, that a Kubernetes name refuses the name and to write it in lower case; the lower-case need, the configuration need STEGO_STORE_MODE and the configuration need STEGO_STORE_REGION of the component to be accepted and to load; and LoadRequirements to refuse Orders_Database and name a capital letter and '_'.
notes: Security re-review of #370, L4; #375 security review L4 (a configuration need of a component keeps the name of its variable, as LoadRequirements accepts it). Mutations caught (2026-11-16): with each new check removed, and with the configuration need held to a Kubernetes name, the test fails.

title: The platform requirements load only with a service name that is a DNS label and components and readers that are plain names
when: The test writes the platform requirements of one component, then loads them once as written, once with a reader of runtime-configuration and its group, and once for each edit: a service name with a capital or a terminal escape, a component with a space or a new line, a reader with a terminal escape, of 129 letters or with a new line in its group.
then: Expects the written file and the grouped reader to load, and each edited file to be refused with a message that says what the name must be.
notes: Env check prints the service, the components and the readers of a file that a person can edit, so LoadRequirements holds them to plain names (#331 security review, F2).

title: The requirements state the variable of a topic or an issuer and the issuer that the declaration fixes, and refuse one of another kind or that no component reads
when: Writes and loads the requirements of a component with an identity issuer need that names its variable and the issuer setting; derives them again with no issuer setting; then with a variable on a secret need, a value on a topic, a variable that no component reads, a secret variable, a value that is not a setting and an issuer that is not https; and loads files edited to a variable not in the list, a secret variable, an http value and a value on a topic.
then: Expects the requirement to hold the variable and the resolved issuer, no value when the setting is not given, and each fault to be refused at derivation and at load with its reason.

title: The written platform requirements hold no value that differs per environment
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set.
then: Expects each entry of the platform requirements file to hold only a kind, a name, a shape and the component that needs it, and the file to hold no secret value, host name, IP address, address range or namespace.
notes: Check the fields of each entry against the fields a requirement may have, not only search for known values, so that a value of a sort the statement does not name is also caught. The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: A component need that holds a host name stops the apply, which names the component and the need and writes nothing
when: In the registry copy, the postgres-adapter component's need orders-database holds the host name db.prod.example.com. stego apply runs on the service of the test data set.
then: Expects stego apply to exit non-zero, naming postgres-adapter, orders-database and the host name field. Expects the project folder and its generation record to be byte-identical to before the run.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: Two applies of the same declaration and registry write the same platform requirements bytes
when: stego apply runs on two copies of the service of the test data set, in two folders with other paths, with other environment variables and at other times.
then: Expects the two platform requirements files to be byte-identical.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: A second apply with no change leaves the platform requirements as they are
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set, then runs again with no change.
then: Expects the platform requirements file after the second run to be byte-identical to the file after the first run.
notes: The requirement says that the file is the same; that a second apply changes nothing at all, its modification time included, is ST-GEN-UC04-R01, and this test does not assert it. The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: Two applies of the same declaration and registry write the same reference bytes
when: stego apply runs on two copies of the service of the test data set, with other environment variables.
then: Expects the two environment variable references to be the same bytes.

title: Two components that state one need with different kinds stop the apply, which names both and the need and writes nothing
when: In the registry copy, the Kafka producer states the need orders-database as a topic, and postgres-adapter states it as a secret. stego apply runs on the service of the test data set.
then: Expects stego apply to exit non-zero, naming both components and orders-database. Expects no file of the project folder to change and no generation record to be written.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: Two components that state one need with different shapes stop the apply, which names both and the need and writes nothing
when: In the registry copy, the Kafka producer states the secret orders-database with the key dsn, and postgres-adapter states it with the keys url and password. stego apply runs on the service of the test data set.
then: Expects stego apply to exit non-zero, naming both components and orders-database. Expects no file of the project folder to change and no generation record to be written.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: A need with the name of a listed environment variable is refused, naming the component, the need and the variable
when: DeriveRequirements runs on components that state a configuration need with the name of a listed variable: DATABASE_URL, which is secret, from another component; DATABASE_URL_FILE of the same component; and the optional BROKERS. Then LoadRequirements reads platform requirements in which a configuration requirement has the name DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_URL_FILE or BROKER_TOKEN, a required secret variable.
then: Expects each to be refused, naming the component, the need, the variable with its kind and the components that read it. Expects the configuration need of a required variable that is not secret, and a need of another name, to be written and to load.
notes: #378 security review L1: a configuration need DATABASE_URL let env check meet it with the credential given as a plain configuration value. #380 security review L1: the case of the required secret variable BROKER_TOKEN proves the clause 'not secret' of the exception in LoadRequirements; DATABASE_URL is optional, so the clause 'required' refuses it first. Mutations caught (2026-11-16): with no check in DeriveRequirements, with no check in LoadRequirements, with LoadRequirements refusing the derived configuration need too, with LoadRequirements accepting a configuration requirement of a secret or optional variable, and with no clause 'not secret' in the exception, the test fails.

title: Applying the plan refuses a hand edit of the platform requirements and names the file
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then one line of the platform requirements file is changed by hand, and stego apply runs again.
then: Expects the second run to exit non-zero, naming the platform requirements file as edited by hand, and to write nothing.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: The drift check names a hand edit of the platform requirements and fails
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then one line of the platform requirements file is changed by hand, and stego drift runs.
then: Expects stego drift to exit non-zero and to name the platform requirements file as drifted.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: A need changes in the platform requirements when the declaration or the registry changes, and not when a fill changes
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then a fill of the service gets a new call that names the environment variable EXTRA_TOKEN and does not read the environment (ST-DLV-Q06 (A)), and stego apply runs; then the declaration takes out the Kafka producer and stego apply runs; then the registry copy adds the key sslmode to the secret of postgres-adapter and stego apply runs.
then: Expects the second run to leave the platform requirements file byte-identical. Expects the third run to take the topic order-events out of the file and change no other entry, and the fourth to add the key sslmode to the secret orders-database and change no other entry.
notes: The fill change is the case that catches a derivation that reads the service's code: the use case's goal is that the platform knows the needs without reading the code. With ST-DLV-UC01-R03-T02 and ST-DLV-UC01-R05-T01, this shows that a need changes only through the declaration or the registry. The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: Applying the plan refuses a hand edit of the reference and names the file
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then a row is added to deploy/environment-variables.md by hand, and stego apply runs again.
then: Expects the second apply to exit non-zero, naming deploy/environment-variables.md as hand-edited.

title: Apply refuses a deploy folder that is a symbolic link and writes nothing through it
when: For a new project of the test data set, once with deploy and once with deploy/base as a symbolic link to an empty folder out of the project, stego apply runs.
then: Expects each apply to be refused with a message that names the symbolic link, no file in the folder that the link names, and no record written.
notes: The platform requirements, the base and the reference file are in deploy/; a link there must not let apply write out of the project folder (#331 security review, F4).

title: Applying the plan writes every environment variable of the active set in the platform requirements, in name order, with its facts
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set.
then: Expects the environment list in name order with at least 40 variables, LOG_LEVEL required with its allowed values and reader, the pool lifetime with its default and range, the default of STEGO_AUTH_ISSUER filled from the declared issuer, DATABASE_URL secret with no default, and no variable of a component that the service does not use.

title: A default from a setting that breaks the variable's type or allowed values stops the apply
when: postgres-adapter declares an integer variable whose default is the setting schema_generation, which the declaration gives the text tables-v1, and stego apply runs.
then: Expects stego apply to exit non-zero, naming postgres-adapter, the variable, the setting and that the value is not an integer, and no file of the project folder to change.

title: Apply marks each variable that the start guard refuses, and validate and apply warn on a secret source that they do not keep
when: stego validate and then stego apply run on the service of the test data set, whose registry copy states the secret orders-database with the keys url and password only.
then: Expects each run to warn on standard error with the variables STEGO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL and STEGO_WORKER_DATABASE_URL, the need orders-database and the keys migration-url and worker-url, and not on DATABASE_URL; each variable of the platform requirements to be marked refused at start exactly when the start guard refuses it, at least 20 of them; and the base to wire none of them.
notes: ST-DLV-Q19 (A).

title: With --strict, validate, plan and apply refuse a secret source that they do not keep, and write nothing
when: stego validate, stego validate --json, stego plan and stego apply run with --strict on the service of the test data set, whose registry copy states the secret orders-database with the keys url and password only; then stego validate runs without --strict; then the service is applied without --strict and committed, an optional field is added so that add steps are pending, and stego plan, stego plan --strict and stego apply --strict run against the commit; then stego apply --strict runs on the service with the shipped registry.
then: Expects each --strict run to fail, to name --strict, each variable, need and key that it does not keep and how to go on, to warn on none, and to write no deploy, .stego or out folder; the run without --strict to warn and pass; with add steps pending, plan without --strict to list the steps and warn, plan --strict and apply --strict to refuse with the secret source, list no step and change no file, and apply to say that it wrote the old service.yaml back; and the shipped registry to pass --strict with no warning.
notes: Security re-review of #370, L3; #375 security review L1 (plan --strict with add steps ran only the declaration checks) and its test gaps. Mutations caught (2026-11-16): with the --strict check removed, with the check plan of stego plan with add steps removed, and without the message of the restored declaration, the test fails.

title: The list carries the group of one of of each variable, and a group of one variable, of two components or with a required variable is refused
when: Writes and loads the platform requirements of a component with DATABASE_URL and DATABASE_URL_FILE in the group database-url; then of the components changed in one way each: a group of one variable, a group of two components, a required variable in the group, a group name with '_', and a second statement of DATABASE_URL_FILE with no group; then loads the written file with a group of one variable and with a required variable in the group.
then: Expects the list to give each variable of the pair one_of database-url; each change to be refused with the variable and the reason, the second statement as a conflict of the two sources on the group of one of; and LoadRequirements to refuse each changed file.
notes: ST-DLV-Q09 (A). Mutations caught (2026-11-16): with each new check removed, the test fails.

title: The platform requirements leave out a variable whose runtime package the generated service does not import
when: The variables DATABASE_URL, STEGO_WORKER_DATABASE_URL read with service, and STEGO_KAFKA_TOPIC read with outbox/kafkaoutbox are filtered by the runtime packages that three sets of generated files import: a browser-service that imports none, a service that also imports runtime/service and runtime/servicex, and one that also imports runtime/outbox/kafkaoutbox.
then: Expects only DATABASE_URL for the browser-service; DATABASE_URL and STEGO_WORKER_DATABASE_URL when runtime/service is imported, so servicex counts as no import of service; and all three when kafkaoutbox is imported too.
notes: Decision on ST-SUP-Q161 (a), walkthrough 7, B6: the Deployment of the browser-service portal wired the worker and relay connection strings and the query cursor key, which only the runtime package service reads, and the portal imports no runtime package.

title: The reference has one section for each reader in name order and one row for each variable in name order, rendered from the list alone
when: Writes the platform requirements and the reference of three sources.
then: Expects the sections and the rows in name order, a row with the facts and the example of the first reader, a secret row with its name and facts alone, and the reference to be the rendering of the derived list byte for byte.

title: A text of the list cannot break a row of the reference
when: Writes the reference with a description that holds a pipe, a backtick and markup, and an example that holds a pipe.
then: Expects each row to have eight cells.

title: Applying the plan writes deploy/environment-variables.md from the list, with one section for each component
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set.
then: Expects the plan to list deploy/environment-variables.md, one row for each variable of the platform requirements, and the sections of health-check, postgres-adapter and rh-sso-auth.

title: The reference names the group of one of of each variable, and lists each group with its variables
when: Writes the reference of the components of ST-DLV-UC01-R06-T05, and of the component with no group alone.
then: Expects the Required cell of DATABASE_URL and DATABASE_URL_FILE to be one of database-url, of BROKERS no, a section Groups of one of with the row database-url and its two variables and the text that the key of the Secret of DATABASE_URL is the one value of its group and never the *_FILE variable, and no such section or text when the list has no group.
notes: ST-DLV-Q09 (A); #375 security review L3. Mutation caught (2026-11-16): without the section of groups, the test fails.

title: No secret value, secret default or secret setting reaches a file that apply writes, or a refusal
when: The secret setting connection_string of postgres-adapter holds the canary text in the declaration, and the process environment of stego apply holds it in DATABASE_URL, PGPASSWORD and a path; stego apply runs. Then, each in a new registry copy, a component declares a secret variable with a default or an example of the canary text, a need name of the secret setting, and a variable that is not secret whose default is the secret setting, and a runtime-configuration secret field states a default of the canary text; stego apply runs each time. Last, stego env check runs on the written requirements with environment files whose secrets hold the canary text.
then: Expects no file that apply writes and no output to hold the canary text, no secret variable with a default or allowed values, each later apply to be refused, naming the component, with no canary text and no changed file, and no output of stego env check to hold the canary text.

title: Two sources that state one variable with different facts are refused, naming both sources and the variable
when: Derives the platform requirements with one variable of two components that differ in the type, the required flag, the default, the secret flag or the allowed values in turn, then with a declaration field of one name with a component variable.
then: Expects each derivation to be refused with no file, naming both components, the variable and the fact, and the last one naming the group of the declaration.

title: Two components that state one variable with different facts stop the apply, which names both and the variable and writes nothing
when: postgres-adapter also declares LOG_LEVEL as optional with a default, and stego apply runs.
then: Expects stego apply to exit non-zero, naming health-check, postgres-adapter, LOG_LEVEL and the required flag, and no file of the project folder to change.

title: The environment check names each unmet requirement with what is missing, and fails
when: In the environment file, the secret orders-database loses the key password and the egress payments is taken out. stego env check runs.
then: Expects it to exit non-zero and to name the secret orders-database with the missing key password and the egress payments as missing, and to name no other requirement as unmet.
notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: The environment check passes when the environment file meets each requirement
when: stego env check runs on the files of the test data set as they are.
then: Expects it to exit 0 and to report that the environment meets each requirement, with no requirement named as unmet.
notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: The check prints each text of a file escaped, so that a file cannot forge a line
when: The engine of the backing store holds a carriage return, an escape sequence that forges a met line, and a right-to-left override.
then: Expects the check to fail, naming the backing store, with no control or bidirectional character in the output and the escape shown as \u{001B}.

title: A wider grant meets its requirement and prints a notice
when: The environment file admits the pod security level baseline and grants the verbs get and list, where the service needs restricted and get.
then: Expects the check to pass and to print a notice for the pod security level and for the extra verb list.

title: An error of the check is printed escaped too
when: The secret orders-database states one key name that holds a right-to-left override twice.
then: Expects the check to fail, naming the environment file, with the character shown as \u{202E} and never as it is.

title: The environment check refuses an image named by tag
when: In the environment file, the image is named by the tag latest. stego env check runs.
then: Expects it to exit non-zero, naming the image value and that it must be named by digest.
notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: The environment check refuses a secret without a key that its requirement names
when: In the environment file, the secret orders-database has the key url only. stego env check runs.
then: Expects it to exit non-zero, naming the secret orders-database and the key password.
notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: A secret key with an empty or null value counts as missing
when: The key password of the secret orders-database gets the empty text, no value, null, a text of one space, a text of white space only, an empty map and an empty list in turn.
then: Expects each check to fail, naming the secret orders-database and the key password.
notes: #378 security review L3: a key whose value was white space, {} or [] counted as given. Mutations caught (2026-11-16): with white space not trimmed, with an empty map or list not empty, and with an empty list not empty, the test fails.

title: A secret environment variable given as a plain configuration value is of the wrong type
when: The environment file gives the secret variable DATABASE_URL the canary text as a configuration value; then a text of one space.
then: Expects each check to fail with a wrong type row for configuration DATABASE_URL that says it is secret, and no canary text in the output.
notes: #380 security review L2: a value of white space only of a secret variable is still a secret given as configuration. Mutation caught (2026-11-16): with the white space row before the secret row, the test fails.

title: Each configuration value has the type, the allowed values and the range of its variable
when: The environment file gives GOMAXPROCS (integer, 1 to 1024) the values eighty, 2000 and 0, JWK_CERT_URL (url) an ftp URL and a host name with no scheme, the required LOG_LEVEL (debug, info, warn, error) the value loud and the required STEGO_SPICEDB_ENDPOINT (address) an https URL, one at a time; then values of the right type inside their ranges.
then: Expects each first check to fail with wrong type, naming the variable, its type and the rule that the value breaks, and the last check to pass.
notes: Walkthrough 3, G5. A url value must be an HTTPS URL (ST-DLV-Q08).

title: Each entry has the shape of its requirement kind
when: The environment file gives the egress payments an address with a scheme and a path, the cluster permission read-config-maps an unknown verb, and then a resource name with spaces, one at a time.
then: Expects each check to fail with wrong type and to name the entry and the shape rule that it breaks.

title: A port outside 1 to 65535 fails the check, and every variable that is a port states that range
when: The environment file gives PORT the values 70000 and 0, then 1, 8443 and 65535, one at a time; then the test reads each component of the registry and finds each integer variable named PORT or ending in _PORT.
then: Expects 70000 and 0 to fail the check as of the wrong type, naming PORT and the bound it passes, and 1, 8443 and 65535 to pass. Expects each port variable of the registry to state the range 1 to 65535, and at least one such variable.
notes: Walkthrough 4: PORT: 70000 passed the check because PORT stated no range.

title: The check refuses a topic or an issuer that differs from the variable that carries it or from the issuer that the declaration fixes
when: Adds to the requirements of ST-DLV-TD02 the variable STEGO_KAFKA_TOPIC on the topic need, and the variable STEGO_AUTH_ISSUER with the fixed issuer on the issuer need; checks the environment file, the file with the same issuer in STEGO_AUTH_ISSUER, then with another topic in the variable, another topic in the need, another issuer than the fixed one, another issuer in the variable, and the topic given by STEGO_KAFKA_TOPIC_FILE.
then: Expects the agreeing files and the file form to meet the requirements, and each other file to give one row of the wrong type for the topic or the issuer that names the variable or the fixed issuer.

title: The environment check does not read secret values, and shows none, whether it passes or fails
when: stego env check runs on the files of the test data set, whose secret values are each the canary text CANARY-SECRET-VALUE; then once for each of two changes to the value of each secret key: the number 0 and a map with one entry; then on a copy in which the secret orders-database has the key url only, with the canary text as its value. An empty value counts as missing (ST-DLV-UC02-R02-T03).
then: Expects the first four runs to exit 0 with the same output bytes. Expects the last run to exit non-zero, naming the secret orders-database and the key password. Expects no output of any run, on standard output or standard error, to hold the canary text.
notes: A check that reads a value gives another result when the value changes type; a check that names a failed secret is where a value most often leaks into a message, so the failed run is the one that most needs the canary. stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: The environment check changes no file, whether it passes or fails
when: stego env check runs on the files of the test data set; then on a copy in which one requirement is unmet.
then: Expects the hash and the modification time of each file in the folder to be the same after each run as before it, and no file to be added.
notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: An environment file that cannot be read is a failed check that names the file and the place
when: The environment file is changed so that it is not valid YAML at line 4. stego env check runs; then it runs on an environment file path that does not exist.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero, naming the file, and for the first run line 4. Expects no output to say that the environment meets the requirements.
notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: Platform requirements that cannot be read or have an unknown shape are a failed check that names the file and the place
when: stego env check runs with a --requirements path that does not exist; then the platform requirements file is changed so that its schema version is 99, and the check runs; then so that its requirements are a map in place of a list, and the check runs.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero and to name the requirements file; the second and the third to name the field that is wrong. Expects no output to say that the environment meets the requirements.
notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: An environment file of an unknown shape is a failed check that names the place
when: In the environment file, the secrets are a list of text in place of a map of entries. stego env check runs.
then: Expects it to exit non-zero, naming the environment file and the path of the secrets field. Expects no output to say that the environment meets the requirements.
notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: A file that is not a regular file is a failed check
when: The environment file is a named pipe.
then: Expects the check to fail at once, naming the environment file and that it is not a regular file.

title: The help and the documentation give the environment schema, each with an example that the check reads
when: Runs stego env check --help, and reads docs/environment-file.md, and checks the example of each with platform requirements of the service tasks that state nothing.
then: Expects the help to exit with no error and name docs/environment-file.md, the help and the document to name each field of the environment schema, and the check to read each example with no error and no value of a wrong type.
notes: Walkthrough 3, item 6: the schema was only in internal/delivery and its test data. The refusal of a file that is not a map now also names the help and the document.

title: A value that no requirement names is listed as unused, and the check still passes
when: The environment file gets the secret legacy-cache and the configuration value LOG_FORMAT, which no requirement names. stego env check runs.
then: Expects it to exit 0, to report that the environment meets each requirement, and to list secret legacy-cache and configuration LOG_FORMAT as unused.
notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: An unused value does not change why the check fails
when: The environment file gets the configuration value LOG_FORMAT, which no requirement names, and loses the egress payments. stego env check runs.
then: Expects it to exit non-zero, naming the egress payments as the one unmet requirement, and to list LOG_FORMAT as unused, not as a cause of the failure.
notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: An unknown environment variable is listed as unused, and a value of a listed variable is not
when: The environment file gives the configuration values STEGO_UNKNOWN_SETTING and PORT.
then: Expects the check to pass and to list STEGO_UNKNOWN_SETTING alone as unused, as named by no requirement and no listed environment variable.

title: A value is matched to a requirement by its kind and its name
when: The environment file also gives a topic named orders-database, the name of a secret requirement.
then: Expects the check to pass and to list the topic orders-database as unused.

title: A required environment variable with no value fails the check, and is named
when: The environment file gives no value to STEGO_QUERY_CURSOR_KEY_FILE; then DATABASE_URL, whose secret source is the key url of orders-database, is marked required in the platform requirements, the check runs, the key url is removed, and a Secret named DATABASE_URL with the keys url and DATABASE_URL is added; then DATABASE_URL without a secret source is required, and a Secret named DATABASE_URL gives the key value, and then the key DATABASE_URL, whose value is the canary text.
then: Expects the first check to fail naming STEGO_QUERY_CURSOR_KEY_FILE; the check with the key url to pass; the checks without it to fail naming the variable DATABASE_URL, also with the Secret named like the variable; the variable with no source to fail with each key, with a row that says the base wires no value for it and to state a secret source in postgres-adapter; and no canary text in the output.
notes: #375 security review L2: a Secret named like a variable, with any key, was a value. #378 security review L2: the base writes no entry and no envFrom for a secret variable with no source, so no Secret gives it a value. Mutations caught (2026-11-16): with a Secret named like the variable counted for a variable with a source or with no source, and with the generic row in place of the reason, the test fails.

title: An optional variable with no value does not fail the check, and an empty value of a required one does
