when: The check runs on the files of the test data set, which give PORT no value; then STEGO_QUERY_CURSOR_KEY_FILE gets the empty text, a text of two spaces and a tab in turn; then the optional PORT gets a text of two spaces and a tab, and the empty text, null and no value, in turn.
then: Expects the first check to pass with no word of PORT, and each check of STEGO_QUERY_CURSOR_KEY_FILE to fail, naming it as empty, and the checks of white space also as of the wrong type. Expects each check of PORT with white space to fail with a wrong type row for configuration PORT that says it is white space only, and each check of PORT with the empty text, null or no value to pass.
notes: #378 security review L3: a value of white space only counted as given. #380 security review L2: such a value of an optional variable then skipped the type check, but the service reads the text as it is, so the check now gives it a wrong type row, for required and optional variables. Mutations caught (2026-11-16): with white space not trimmed, with no wrong type row for white space, and with the empty text or null counted as white space, the test fails.

title: The environment check fails for a group of one of with no value or more than one, and names the group and how to give each variable
when: Checks environment files against the platform requirements of ST-DLV-UC01-R06-T05 with the pair BROKERS and BROKERS_FILE of the group brokers, which has no secret source: the key url of the Secret orders-database; neither that key nor a DATABASE_URL_FILE; BROKERS_FILE alone; an empty BROKERS alone; and both BROKERS and BROKERS_FILE.
then: Expects the row group database-url to be met for the first and missing for the second, with the group and the key url of orders-database as DATABASE_URL or DATABASE_URL_FILE with the Component secret-files; the row group brokers to be met for the third, missing for the fourth with each way to give a variable, and of the wrong type for the fifth with the two variables and that the service refuses them together; no row shows a secret value.
notes: ST-DLV-Q09 (A). The fixture of ST-DLV-TD02 gives one variable of each shipped group. Mutations caught (2026-11-16): with the check of no value, of more than one value, or of the key of the secret source removed, the test fails.

title: The environment check counts a value of a group as the base wires it: the key of the secret source in both forms, never a *_FILE value or a Secret named like the variable
when: Checks environment files against the platform requirements of ST-DLV-UC02-R06-T03: the key url of orders-database with a DATABASE_URL_FILE that is not an absolute path; DATABASE_URL_FILE without the key url; a Secret DATABASE_URL_FILE with the key url; a Secret named DATABASE_URL with the keys url and DATABASE_URL without the key url; and orders-database without the key url. Then, with DATABASE_URL without a secret source, a Secret DATABASE_URL with the key DATABASE_URL, the key url, no key, and an empty key DATABASE_URL; and DATABASE_URL_FILE alone.
then: Expects the row group database-url to be met, with a passing check, when the key url is given, and missing without it, also with DATABASE_URL_FILE or a Secret named DATABASE_URL; a notice for each DATABASE_URL_FILE value that says the base never wires it, the key url of orders-database that gives it as DATABASE_URL or as the file with the Component secret-files, and to remove it; no notice when the file gives none; no secret value in a row or a notice; and, with no source, the group missing with each Secret DATABASE_URL, with a row that says the base does not wire DATABASE_URL and a notice that names the reader to state a secret source, and met by DATABASE_URL_FILE alone with no such notice.
notes: #375 security review L3 (a DATABASE_URL_FILE always failed as more than one with the shipped postgres-adapter) and L2 (a Secret named like a variable, with any key, was a value). #378 security review L2 (a secret variable with no source was given by a Secret of its name through envFrom, which the base never writes). The base wires the pair from the key of the Secret only (baseEnvironment, jobEnvironment). Mutations caught (2026-11-16): with the *_FILE form counted, without the notice, with the notice not skipping the type check, with a Secret named like the variable counted, with any key or no key of a Secret of its name counted, with the key of its name counted for a variable with no source, without the notice of a variable with no source, and without the reason in the row of the group, the test fails.

title: The hosted CI pipeline runs each of the five STEGO checks before it releases the image
when: A push of the service of the test data set runs the generated pipeline on the hosted CI provider.
then: Expects the run to show drift, vet, test, the reproducible build and the executable match each as passed, in the STEGO checks step, before the publish step, and the image to be published only after they pass.
notes: Runs on the developer workstation against the local stand-in of the hosted CI provider of ST-DLV-TD04 (ST-STD-LOCAL). A run on the real provider MAY follow as a second proof.

title: The Konflux pipeline runs each of the five STEGO checks before it releases the image
when: A push of the service of the test data set starts the generated PipelineRun on Konflux.
then: Expects the pipeline run to have a STEGO checks task whose results show drift, vet, test, the reproducible build and the executable match each as passed, and the image to be released only after that task passes.
notes: Runs on the developer workstation against the local Konflux stand-in of ST-DLV-TD05 (Tekton Pipelines and Tekton Chains in a local kind cluster that run the pinned Konflux standard pipeline bundle) (ST-STD-LOCAL). A run on a real Konflux tenant MAY follow as a second proof.

title: On the hosted CI provider, a failure of any one STEGO check releases no image
when: Five pushes run the generated pipeline on the hosted CI provider, each with one change that makes one check fail: drift (a generated file edited by hand), vet (a vet finding in a fill), test (a fill test that fails), the reproducible build (an input that makes the second build differ), and the executable match (an image whose executable differs from the record).
then: Expects each run to fail at the check that the change breaks, naming that check, and to publish no image to the test image repository.
notes: Runs on the developer workstation against the local stand-in of the hosted CI provider of ST-DLV-TD04 (ST-STD-LOCAL). A run on the real provider MAY follow as a second proof. Five changes, one per check, so that a check that a pipeline leaves out is caught.

title: On Konflux, a failure of any one STEGO check releases no image
when: Five pushes start the generated PipelineRun on Konflux, each with one change that makes one check fail: drift (a generated file edited by hand), vet (a vet finding in a fill), test (a fill test that fails), the reproducible build (an input that makes the second build differ), and the executable match (an image whose executable differs from the record).
then: Expects each pipeline run to fail at the STEGO checks task, naming the check that the change breaks, and no image of the run to be released for delivery.
notes: Runs on the developer workstation against the local Konflux stand-in of ST-DLV-TD05 (Tekton Pipelines and Tekton Chains in a local kind cluster that run the pinned Konflux standard pipeline bundle) (ST-STD-LOCAL). A run on a real Konflux tenant MAY follow as a second proof.

title: The delivery check refuses an image whose executable differs by one byte from the recorded one
when: stego delivery check runs on the Konflux image of the test data set with its build record and its digest; then on a copy of that image in which one byte of the executable is changed.
then: Expects the first run to pass the executable match. Expects the second run to exit non-zero, naming the executable match, the recorded digest and the digest found.
notes: stego delivery check runs as a child process with --image, --record and --record-sha256.

title: On Konflux, the generated Containerfile builds hermetically from the prefetched modules to the recorded executable
when: A push of the service of the test data set starts the generated PipelineRun with the hermetic build and the Go module prefetch.
then: Expects the build task to succeed with the network off, its final image to be on scratch, its builder image to be the archetype's Go SDK by digest, and the executable digest to equal the one in the build record of stego build for the same revision.
notes: CI or the cluster only, never on the developer workstation: it runs against the local Konflux stand-in of ST-DLV-TD05 (Tekton Pipelines and Tekton Chains in a kind cluster that run the pinned Konflux standard pipeline bundle). A run on a real Konflux tenant MAY follow as a second proof. ST-DLV-INV07-T proves the same Containerfile with buildah alone, and ST-DLV-UC03-R04-T03 holds its shape on every local run.

title: On Konflux, a prefetched module that does not match the module checksums stops the build
when: The push changes go.sum so that the checksum of one module does not match the module that the prefetch gives. The generated PipelineRun runs.
then: Expects the prefetch or the build task to fail, naming the module, and no image to be released.
notes: CI or the cluster only, never on the developer workstation: it runs against the local Konflux stand-in of ST-DLV-TD05 (Tekton Pipelines and Tekton Chains in a kind cluster that run the pinned Konflux standard pipeline bundle). ST-DLV-UC03-R04-T03 holds the shape of the Containerfile on every local run.

title: Apply writes the offline Containerfile: a pinned Go build with the network off, then a scratch image that runs as a user that is not root
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then the test reads the Containerfile with its own parser, the record and the base that kustomize builds.
then: Expects the plan to list the Containerfile and the record to track it under project_files; the build stage to be FROM the Go image of appbuild.GoVersion by sha256 digest, to copy the module files and the output folder, to hold no ADD, and to run one build that starts with env -i, sets each setting of the application build with the module proxy off and the prefetched module cache, checks the Go version, runs go mod verify and the arguments of the application build, and fetches nothing; the final stage to be FROM scratch, to copy only from the build stage, to run nothing, to set a numeric user and group that are not root and to start the executable in exec form; and each container of the base to have a read-only root file system.
notes: The test parses the file and does not build it: a real build is ST-DLV-INV07-T, which runs in CI or the cluster only.

title: The Containerfile reads back only as the exact text that apply writes, and a file with more text, another image, a directive or a heredoc is refused
when: WriteContainerfile writes the Containerfile for the output folder out, for out with the fills folder and for gen/service, and LoadContainerfile reads each back; then LoadContainerfile reads the file of out with the fills folder with one change each: a second GOPROXY setting after GOPROXY=off in the build, a fetch before the go command, another Go image named by a digest, a COPY with --from after another flag, a syntax directive, an escape directive, a heredoc in place of the fills folder, another output folder in the build than in the copy, and a changed comment.
then: Expects each written file to read back; each changed file to be refused; a changed comment to be refused as not the file that stego apply writes for the output folder out, with the advice to run stego apply; another image to be refused as not the pinned Go image; and a COPY with --link before --from to be refused as a copy from another image.
notes: Security review of PR #367, L1: the shape checks alone found the build RUN by substrings, took any image named by a digest, looked for --from only at the first flag and did not see parser directives or heredocs, which BuildKit obeys. LoadContainerfile now holds the file to the exact bytes of the renderer for the source folders that the build stage copies. Mutations caught (agents/fu-standing/mut-containerfile.log): the exact bytes check removed (six changes accepted); the builder image check removed (the message check); --from looked for at the first flag only (the message check).

title: Apply copies each local module folder that go.mod replaces a module with into the build stage, and names a replacement out of the project
when: After a first stego apply on the service of the test data set, go.mod gets replace directives to two folders of the project (one of them given twice and one with a module in it), to a folder in the output folder, to a folder with a space, to one that starts with '_', to a folder out of the project and to a path out of the project with a terminal escape and a new line; then stego apply runs again.
then: Expects the Containerfile to read back, its build stage to copy the output folder and then each local module folder of the project once, in path order, and no other folder; and the plan to give a line with the quoted path for each replacement that it does not copy, with no terminal escape or new line of go.mod in it.
notes: stego build reads the local module folders from its source snapshot; without them in the build stage the offline build fails or builds another executable (walkthrough-4).

title: The local module replacements give each folder that the build stage copies once, and a quoted plan line for each that it cannot copy
when: ModuleFolders gets, for the output folder gen/service and a fills folder, replacements to two folders of the project, a module in one of them, a folder in the output folder or in fills, the project folder, a folder that holds the output folder, a folder with a space, one that starts with '_', and an absolute, a drive and a parent path.
then: Expects the two folders once, in path order, a plan line with the quoted path for each of the six that it cannot copy, and a Containerfile that WriteContainerfile accepts for the folders.
notes: A layout that stego build accepts must not make apply fail (security review of PR #395, L2).

title: A hosted CI image is signed by the keyless identity of the pinned shared pipeline, and by no other
when: A push runs the generated pipeline on the hosted CI provider. The signature of the published image is verified against the identity of the shared pipeline at the pinned commit, then against the identity of the service's own workflow.
then: Expects the first verification to pass, with the certificate's workflow reference at the pinned commit, and the second to fail.
notes: Runs on the developer workstation against the local stand-in of the hosted CI provider of ST-DLV-TD04, whose keyless signing stand-in issues a short-lived certificate that names the workflow that the local runner ran, at its commit, as the provider's keyless signing does (ST-STD-LOCAL). A run on the real provider MAY follow as a second proof.

title: A Konflux image is signed by the Tekton Chains key
when: A push starts the generated PipelineRun on Konflux. The signature of the image is verified with the Tekton Chains public key that the registry names, then with another public key.
then: Expects the first verification to pass and the second to fail.
notes: Runs on the developer workstation against the local Konflux stand-in of ST-DLV-TD05 (Tekton Pipelines and Tekton Chains in a local kind cluster that run the pinned Konflux standard pipeline bundle) (ST-STD-LOCAL). A run on a real Konflux tenant MAY follow as a second proof.

title: The delivery check refuses an image signed by a signer that is not its provider's trusted signer
when: stego delivery check runs on a copy of the hosted image of the test data set signed with the test Tekton Chains key, and on a copy signed with a key the registry does not name.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero, naming the signer found and the trusted signer of the provider that built the image.
notes: An image that carries a signer of the other provider is the case that catches a check that accepts any trusted signer, not the one of its provider.

title: The delivery check passes an image that also carries another signature, and refuses one whose only valid signature is another signer's
when: Make two copies of the hosted image of the test data set, which the trusted signer of the hosted CI provider signed. Add to the first copy a second signature by a test key K3 that the registry does not name, as a mirror or a promotion adds one. On the second copy, replace the trusted signer's signature with one over another digest, so that it does not verify, and add a valid signature by K3. Run stego delivery check on each copy.
then: Expects the run on the first copy to exit 0, with the signature check passed and naming the trusted signer. Expects the run on the second copy to exit non-zero, naming the trusted signer of the hosted CI provider as the signer with no valid signature, and not reporting the image as signed.
notes: Decision on review item R1 of the Delivering test plan, reading b: only the trusted signer's signature counts. The first copy catches a check that refuses an image with any other signature. The second copy catches a check that passes an image when any one of its signatures verifies.

title: Applying the plan writes the delivery policy file from the declaration and the registry's advisories
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then the registry copy gets an advisory that withdraws the digest of one component that the declaration uses, and stego apply runs again.
then: Expects the first run to write the delivery policy file at the path that the CI file passes to the pipeline, with the trusted signer and the image targets of the declaration. Expects the second run to change the policy file so that it refuses the withdrawn digest, naming the advisory.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: The delivery check evaluates the policy file that the pipeline carries
when: stego apply runs on a copy of the service of the test data set with a registry copy whose ci-pipeline component names the test key K2 as the trusted signer of the hosted CI provider, and its delivery policy file is kept. With the original registry, and the hosted image signed by the trusted signer of that registry: stego delivery check runs on the image with --policy and --policy-sha256 naming the delivery policy file that stego apply wrote from the original registry and its digest; then again with --policy and --policy-sha256 naming the kept policy file and its digest.
then: Expects the first run to pass and to name the policy file it evaluated. Expects the second run to exit non-zero, naming the signer found in the image, K2 as the trusted signer that the policy names, and the kept policy file.
notes: The registry does not change between the two runs, so a check that derives its own policy from the registry, and not from the file that the pipeline carries, gives the same result twice and fails the test. Decision on review item R2 of the Delivering test plan: the check takes --policy and --policy-sha256, as it takes the build record (ST-DLV-CLI01). Decision on ST-DLV-Q02: the platform's gate is the platform's to prove, so this test proves STEGO's half only.

title: The delivery check refuses a policy file whose digest is not the trusted digest, before any check, and the CI file passes the policy file and its digest
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set. Read the delivery check step of the hosted CI file and of the Konflux PipelineRun. Then change one byte of the delivery policy file that apply wrote, and run stego delivery check on the hosted image with --policy naming that file and --policy-sha256 the digest of the file before the change.
then: Expects the delivery check step of each CI file to pass --policy with the path of the policy file that apply wrote and --policy-sha256 with that file's SHA-256 digest. Expects the run to exit non-zero, naming the policy file and the two digests, and to print no result of any image check.
notes: Decision on review item R2 of the Delivering test plan, reading a. A check that reads the policy file and does not compare its digest passes the changed file and fails the test. That no image check runs catches a check that compares the digest after it evaluates the policy.

title: Applying the plan takes each pin and the trusted signer of the CI file from the registry's ci-pipeline component
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then on a copy whose delivery stanza names Konflux.
then: Expects each pinned reference and the trusted signer in the hosted CI file and in the Konflux PipelineRun to equal what the ci-pipeline component names.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: A declaration that sets a pipeline reference is refused, naming the path
when: The delivery stanza of the declaration sets a pipeline reference. stego apply runs.
then: Expects stego apply to exit non-zero, naming the path of the field in the declaration as not declared, and no file of the project folder to change.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: A declaration that sets a trusted signer is refused, naming the path
when: The delivery stanza of the declaration sets a trusted signer. stego apply runs.
then: Expects stego apply to exit non-zero, naming the path of the field in the declaration as not declared, and no file of the project folder to change.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: A ci-pipeline version that changes one pin changes only that pin in each service's CI file
when: stego apply runs on two copies of the service of the test data set, one for each provider, and each is committed; then the registry copy gets a ci-pipeline version that changes only the shared pipeline commit and the Konflux bundle digest, and stego apply runs on each copy.
then: Expects git diff of each CI file to show only the changed line that holds the pin. Expects no other generated file to change, and the generation record to change only in the hash of the CI file.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: A ci-pipeline component whose reference uses a tag, a branch or a short hash is refused
when: Three runs of stego apply on the service of the test data set, each with a registry copy whose ci-pipeline component pins the shared pipeline by the tag v1.2.0, by the branch main, or by the short hash 0123456.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero, naming the ci-pipeline component and the reference, and no file of the project folder to change.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: A patch to a hand-edited CI file is refused, naming the file, and nothing is written
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set and the result is committed; then the CI file gets one line by hand, and the registry copy gets a ci-pipeline version with a new pin, and stego apply runs.
then: Expects stego apply to exit non-zero, naming the CI file as edited by hand. Expects git status to show only the hand edit, and the generation record to be byte-identical to before the run.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: With leave to replace hand-edited files, the patch replaces the hand-edited CI file
when: As in ST-DLV-UC04-R04-T01, but stego apply runs with the statement that the run may replace hand-edited files.
then: Expects stego apply to exit 0, the CI file to hold the new pin and not the hand-edited line, and the generation record to hold the new hash of the CI file.
notes: The command's statement is the one of ST-GEN-UC03-R03; ST-GEN-CLI01 says today that stego apply takes no flag, which the Generating domain must change. The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: For the hosted CI provider, applying the plan writes a CI file that only calls the shared pipeline by full commit and the STEGO checks by pin
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set.
then: Expects the CI file to hold two jobs, the check job and the release job, each of which only calls the platform's shared pipeline at the 40-character commit that the registry names and passes the STEGO checks reference by its pin and the trusted signer, with no step or script of its own; and WritePipeline to refuse a signer that holds an expression or is empty, and a service name that is not a DNS label.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: For Konflux, applying the plan writes a PipelineRun that only references the standard pipeline bundle and the STEGO checks by digest, and builds the offline Containerfile hermetic
when: The delivery stanza of the declaration names Konflux. stego apply runs on the service of the test data set.
then: Expects the PipelineRun to reference the Konflux standard pipeline bundle and the STEGO checks bundle each by the sha256 digest that the registry names, with no inline pipeline, task or script. Expects the parameters dockerfile Containerfile, hermetic true and the prefetch-input of the Go modules of the project folder, and expects the strict read-back to refuse the file with hermetic false, with another dockerfile, with another prefetch-input, with another pipeline name than docker-build, or with a second hermetic parameter.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder. The build parameters close the walkthrough-4 follow-up: the Konflux PipelineRun must pass the dockerfile, hermetic and prefetch-input parameters (ST-DLV-UC03-R04).

title: With no pins for the provider in the registry, applying the plan writes no CI file and says so
when: The delivery stanza names the hosted CI provider, and the registry is the shipped registry, whose ci-pipeline component states no provider yet. stego apply runs on the service of the test data set.
then: Expects apply to exit 0, its plan to say that no CI file is written, and no CI file to be in the project folder.
notes: ST-DLV-Q13 (A) with (C): the shipped component states no provider until the Product owner gives the real values, so no CI file can carry a pin that is not real.

title: A pull request run of the CI file has no write permission, and a push on a feature branch signs nothing
when: The delivery stanza names the hosted CI provider, and the fixture registry holds its pins. stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then a contract fake of GitHub Actions evaluates the if condition of each job of the CI file for a pull request, a push on a feature branch, a push on the default branch and a push of a tag.
then: Expects no job of the pull request run to have a write permission, the push on the feature branch to run no job with id-token write, and the push on the default branch and the push of the tag each to run the release job with id-token write.
notes: ST-DLV-Q16 (A) and the security review of PR #352 (M2).

title: The written Kubernetes base builds with plain kustomize, with no plugin or remote base
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then the pinned kustomize version builds the base with the network off and no plugin or exec option.
then: Expects the build to exit 0, and the kustomization file to list no remote base, no path out of the base folder, no generator or transformer that names a plugin, and no Helm chart.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: The written Kubernetes base sets no replicas, PodDisruptionBudget, namespace, image digest, host name, egress address or secret value
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set, which has an ingress, an egress destination and a secret; then kustomize builds the base.
then: Expects no resource of the build to set replicas or metadata namespace, no PodDisruptionBudget, no image named by digest, no host name in an ingress or route, no address or address range in a network policy, and no Secret data or string data.
notes: Check each resource of the built output, not only the files that STEGO writes today, so that a new resource is also checked. The requirement forbids an image digest; it does not forbid an image name or tag, so the test does not refuse one. The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: The written Kubernetes base names an image that no registry serves, and the plan says each overlay must set the digest
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then kustomize builds the base.
then: Expects each container image to be stego.invalid/orders:set-by-overlay, a name in a reserved domain that fails to pull, and the plan to say that every overlay must set the image by digest.
notes: Security review of PR #351, L2: a bare name would pull docker.io/library/orders when an overlay sets no image.

title: The written Kubernetes base carries the probes that health-check derives
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then kustomize builds the base.
then: Expects each container of the Deployment to have a liveness and a readiness probe at the path and port that health-check derives for the service.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: The written Kubernetes base carries default resources that an overlay can change
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then kustomize builds the base, and then an overlay fixture that patches the memory limit to 1Gi.
then: Expects each container in the base to have CPU, memory and ephemeral storage requests and limits equal to the defaults, and the overlay build to have the memory limit 1Gi with each other default the same.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: The written Kubernetes base always sets the restricted security context and a read-only root file system
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then kustomize builds the base.
then: Expects the pod to run as non-root with the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile and one bounded emptyDir tmp, and each container to allow no privilege escalation, drop every capability, have a read-only root file system and mount tmp at /tmp.
notes: ST-DLV-Q14 (A).

title: A cluster permission that can take over the namespace is refused, and get on secrets names its secrets
when: Derives the platform requirements from a component with one cluster permission need for each of: list and watch on secrets, get on secrets with no resource names, serviceaccounts/token, pods/exec, pods/attach, pods/portforward, pods/proxy, create on pods, and four RBAC resources; then from get on secrets with the resource name {service}-database; then from a secret need with resource names.
then: Expects each sensitive need to be refused, naming the component and the need; the named get on secrets to be accepted with the resource name orders-database; and the secret need with resource names to be refused.
notes: ST-DLV-Q14 (A), the red-team test of the security review of PR #351 (M2).

title: The base writes one environment entry, names only, for each variable the service reads
when: Writes the platform requirements and then the base of the service orders from components with a secret variable with a secret source and its *_FILE form, a secret variable with no source, a path variable that names the file of a secret, a required and an optional variable that are not secret, the console sink of the domain probes, and the port of the probes; then again with a secret source whose key the need does not state.
then: Expects the container to have, in name order, a secretKeyRef to the key url of orders-database with no optional flag, and a configMapKeyRef to the key of its name in orders-config for each other variable, optional for each optional one, and no entry for the *_FILE form, for the secret variable with no source or for STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE (ST-STD-OBS-R03). Expects the second run to keep no secret source and to name no Secret.
notes: ST-DLV-Q18 (A) and ST-DLV-Q19. The fixture also has a secret variable of the migrate mode, which gets no entry, and a service name of 60 characters is refused with the message to use a shorter one (#370 security review L5).

title: No file of the base or of the Component holds a value, and LoadBase refuses an environment entry with one
when: Writes the base of ST-DLV-UC07-R03-T05, whose secret setting, default and example are each the canary text; then LoadBase reads copies whose Deployment has an entry with a value, a value in place of a reference, a field reference, an optional secret, optional false, two references in one entry, one variable twice, a ConfigMap that is not a name, and a hostPath volume (security review of #373, M1).
then: Expects the four files of the base and the three of the Component, no file to hold the canary text, no entry of the base to set a value, and LoadBase to refuse each copy.
notes: ST-DLV-Q18 (A): never a value. LoadBase also refuses an envFrom, and an environment in an init or an ephemeral container (#370 security review L2); no file names the migration key.

title: A kustomize build of the base, and of the base with the Component secret-files, gives exactly one form of each secret
when: Writes the base of ST-DLV-UC07-R03-T05 to a folder, and builds with the kustomize library, plugins off, one overlay of the base and one overlay of the base with the Component deploy/components/secret-files.
then: Expects the base build to have DATABASE_URL and not DATABASE_URL_FILE; the build with the Component to have DATABASE_URL_FILE and the path variable each with only the path of its file under /var/run/secrets/stego, no DATABASE_URL, the other entries as the base writes them, and each secret mounted read-only at its folder with no subPath from a secret volume with the mode 0400, next to tmp.
notes: ST-DLV-Q18 (A). Each secret volume projects only the key that its switched variable reads (#370 security review H1). A run of real pods is not needed: the failure of a missing key (CreateContainerConfigError) is documented in docs/delivery.md.

title: LoadBase accepts the Component secret-files only with its exact kinds and patches
when: LoadBase reads the base of ST-DLV-UC07-R03-T05, then copies whose Component is a Kustomization, has a third patch, lists the patches in the other order, has a resource, patches a Service or another Deployment, sets a value in the removal patch, mounts a secret that is not read-only or with a subPath, has the mode 0644, has a volume of another kind, sets a file out of the secret folder, sets a variable that the removal patch does not remove, leaves out a file, or holds another file.
then: Expects LoadBase to accept the base and to refuse each copy.
notes: ST-DLV-Q18 (A): LoadBase stays strict. Also refused: a volume with no items, a key at another path, and a projected key that no variable reads (#370 security review H1).

title: A variable that the start guard refuses gets no entry in the base, is never required, and the environment check refuses a value for it
when: Writes the platform requirements and the base of ST-DLV-UC07-R03-T05 with the refused variable PGHOST and the allowed GRPC_GO_LOG_SEVERITY_LEVEL; then with PGHOST required; then checks an environment file without PGHOST, one that gives PGHOST a value, and ones that give PGHOST a space, a tab, the empty text and null.
then: Expects only PGHOST to be marked refused at start, the base to wire GRPC_GO_LOG_SEVERITY_LEVEL and not PGHOST, the required PGHOST to be refused, the first check to name no PGHOST row, the second, the space and the tab to name configuration PGHOST as refused at start, without its value, and the empty text and null to name no such row.
notes: Owner delegation, 2026-11-15: an optional ConfigMap key of a refused variable would stop the service (ST-SUP-UC01-R10). #380 security review L2: the start guard refuses each value that is not the empty text, so a value of white space only is refused too. Mutations caught (2026-11-16): with white space counted as no value, with the empty text counted as white space, and with the white space row before the refused row, the test fails.

title: No serving file of the base or of the Component names the credential of the migration job, which has a Secret of its own
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set with the shipped registry as it is, which states the secret needs orders-database and orders-database-owner.
then: Expects the platform requirements to mark STEGO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL and its _FILE form as read by the migrate mode, STEGO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL to take the key url of orders-database-owner, the secret need orders-database to state the keys url and worker-url only, and orders-database-owner the key url. Expects the three files of the migration Job to be written, the Job and its mount patch to name orders-database-owner, and no other file of deploy/base or deploy/components to hold migration-url, STEGO_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL or database-owner.
notes: Red-team test of the security review of #370 (H1). ST-DLV-Q19, least privilege; ST-DLV-Q20, the owner Secret. Mutation caught (2026-11-16): with migration-url back in the keys of {service}-database in the registry, the test fails.

title: A kustomize build of the base with the Components secret-files and fs-group gives files of the mode 0400 to the fsGroup 65532
when: Writes the base of ST-DLV-UC07-R03-T05, which has a migration Job, and builds with the kustomize library an overlay with the Component secret-files alone and one with secret-files and fs-group.
then: Expects the base to hold the three files of the Component fs-group, its kustomization to say never to list it on OpenShift, the build with secret-files alone to set no fsGroup, and the build with the two Components to give the Deployment and the Job the pod securityContext fsGroup 65532, runAsNonRoot and RuntimeDefault, secret volumes of the mode 0400, and no other change.
notes: Security re-review of #370: the base sets no fsGroup, because the OpenShift restricted-v2 SCC refuses a pod that sets one outside its namespace range (orchestrator, under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-16). Mutation caught (2026-11-16): with the fsGroup 1000 in the patches, LoadBase refuses the base and the test fails.

title: LoadBase accepts the Component fs-group only with its exact shape
when: Changes the base of ST-DLV-UC07-R03-T05 in one way each: another fsGroup, a runAsUser, a supplemental group, a container, a hostPath volume, a hostNetwork, a namespace, a patch of another workload or kind, a Kustomization in place of the Component, a patch with a target or options, an inline patch, the patches in the other order, a resource, a file left out or added, and the Component fs-group without the Component secret-files; then writes a base with no migration Job and adds a patch of a Job to it.
then: Expects LoadBase to accept the base as written and to refuse each change with its own reason: the patch that is not of the Deployment or the Job with the fsGroup 65532, the Component that does not list the two patches in order, the Component that does not hold exactly its files, the field that the strict decoder does not know, the Component secret-files that is not there, or the file that is not of the base; and the base with no Job to hold the patch of the Deployment alone.
notes: Mutations caught (2026-11-16): with the check of the fsGroup value, the check of the Component secret-files or the call of loadFSGroup removed, the test fails. The hostPath, hostNetwork, namespace, target, options and inline patch cases are the probes of the #375 security review, which the strict decoder refuses. #378 security review: the test asserts the reason of each refusal; the runAsUser and supplemental group probes were refused only as YAML syntax errors before, and now reach the strict decoder. Mutations caught (2026-11-16): with the patch decoded not strictly, and with the old indent of the runAsUser probe, the test fails.

title: A service name of 57 to 63 characters gets its ConfigMap reference, and a secret name of more than 63 characters is refused with a clear message
when: Writes the platform requirements and the base of a service name of 63 characters with variables that are not secret; then the platform requirements of that service with the secret needs of ST-DLV-UC07-R03-T05; then changes the ConfigMap reference of the base to a name of 254 characters, a name with a capital letter and a name with '_'.
then: Expects the base to take the variable from the ConfigMap <service>-config of 70 characters, the platform requirements to be refused with the secret name, more than the 63 and use a shorter service name, and LoadBase to refuse each changed reference and name a DNS subdomain.
notes: Security re-review of #370, L1: a Secret or ConfigMap name is a DNS subdomain of at most 253 characters, so the ConfigMap reference no longer gives an unclear refusal. Mutation caught (2026-11-16): with the reference held to a DNS label again, the test fails.

title: Applying the plan writes an ApplicationSet whose environment values come from the platform's environment files
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set.
then: Expects an Argo CD ApplicationSet whose template names the service orders and the project orders, whose one source is the platform's overlay at the overlay path parameter, whose files generator lists the platform's environment files at the location the delivery stanza gives, and whose destination cluster and namespace are each a parameter of that generator, with no literal value. Expects the plan and the file header to state the resource line that pulls the base pinned to a commit, and the plan to say that the platform must lock the AppProject. A contract fake of the files generator renders the template from the environment file of ST-DLV-TD02.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: A delivery stanza that names a destination, a namespace or an overlay is refused, naming the path, and nothing is written
when: Three runs of stego apply on the service of the test data set, each with a delivery stanza that also names a destination cluster, a namespace, or an overlay path.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero, naming the path of the field in the declaration as not declared, and no file of the project folder to change.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: The project default and an unknown CI provider are refused by stego validate and stego apply, naming the path
when: Three declarations of the service of the test data set: one whose delivery stanza names the project default, one whose ci is jenkins, and one whose source repository host starts with '-'. stego validate and stego apply run on each.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero and name the path of the field (delivery.argocd.project, delivery.ci, delivery.argocd.source.repo), and no file of the project folder to change.
notes: ST-DLV-Q15 (A) and the security review of PR #355 (M1, L3, L4).

title: With no delivery stanza, applying the plan writes no ApplicationSet, says so, and invents no destination
when: The delivery stanza is taken out of the declaration. stego apply runs on the service of the test data set.
then: Expects stego apply to exit 0, its plan to say that no delivery object is written because the declaration has no delivery stanza, no file with the kind ApplicationSet or Application to be written, and no generated file to name an Argo CD project, a destination or an environment file location.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: The base writes the migration Job of the release, which runs migrate with the restricted pod security and the owner credential alone
when: Writes the platform requirements and the base of the service orders from the components of ST-DLV-UC07-R03-T05, with the owner credential STEGO_MIGRATION_URL in the secret need {service}-database-owner, read by the mode migrate, and the key file STEGO_SPICEDB_KEY_FILE of the secret need {service}-spicedb, at a fixed release digest; then writes the base of the same components with no variable of the mode migrate and no digest.
then: Expects LoadBase to accept the base, and the kustomization to list migration-job.yaml. Expects the batch/v1 Job orders-migrate-0123456789 with exactly the annotations argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync, argocd.argoproj.io/hook-delete-policy: BeforeHookCreation,HookSucceeded and argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "0", exactly the labels app.kubernetes.io/name, part-of and component: migration, backoffLimit 2, activeDeadlineSeconds 7200 and ttlSecondsAfterFinished 600; pods with the label app.kubernetes.io/part-of and no app.kubernetes.io/name, restartPolicy Never, no service account token, no service account name, and runAsNonRoot with the seccomp profile RuntimeDefault and no fsGroup; one container with the image, the security context and the resources of the Deployment and the one argument migrate. Expects STEGO_MIGRATION_URL from the key url of orders-database-owner, the ConfigMap entries of the Deployment for PORT, STEGO_ISSUER, STEGO_SPICEDB_KEY_FILE and STEGO_STORE_TIMEOUT, and no other entry: no DATABASE_URL, PGPASSWORD, STEGO_CURSOR_KEY_FILE, STEGO_MIGRATION_URL_FILE or STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE. Expects no Job in the second base.
notes: ST-DLV-Q20.

title: A kustomize build of the base and of the base with the Component gives the Job its image digest and one form of the owner credential
when: Writes the base of ST-DLV-UC07-R06-T01 to a folder and builds with the kustomize library, plugins off, one overlay that sets the namespace and the image by digest, and one that also lists the Component secret-files.
then: Expects each build to hold one Job and one Deployment, the Job with the image by digest and the namespace, and the selector of the Deployment not to take the pods of the Job. Expects the plain build of the Job to hold STEGO_MIGRATION_URL; the build with the Component to hold STEGO_MIGRATION_URL_FILE at /var/run/secrets/stego/orders-database-owner/url and STEGO_SPICEDB_KEY_FILE at /var/run/secrets/stego/orders-spicedb/preshared-key, each with a value only, no STEGO_MIGRATION_URL, and exactly the volumes tmp, orders-database-owner with the key url and orders-spicedb with the key preshared-key, each of the mode 0400. Expects the Deployment with the Component not to name database-owner or STEGO_MIGRATION_URL.
notes: ST-DLV-Q20. The kustomize library is a test dependency only (ST-DLV-REPO03).

title: A Job name of more than 63 characters and a release that is no digest are refused with a clear message
when: Gives MigrationJobName a service name of 44 characters, then one of 45, then the service orders with an empty release, a short one, an upper-case one and a word; then writes the base of the fixture for the service name of 45 characters; then writes it for orders at another release.
then: Expects the name of 63 characters for the 44 characters, and a refusal that names the 63 characters and the longest service name, 44, for 45; a refusal that names the hex digits for each bad release; a refusal of the base of the long name; and a Job of another name for the other release.
notes: ST-DLV-Q20: a Job name is also the value of the label job-name, a DNS label of at most 63 characters.

title: LoadBase accepts the migration Job only with its exact shape
when: LoadBase reads copies of the base of ST-DLV-UC07-R06-T01 whose Job has, each in turn: an fsGroup, a service account, a service account token, a privilege escalation, a writable root file system, a capability kept, root, no seccomp profile, another argument, restartPolicy OnFailure, no time to live, no limits, no cpu limit, no memory request, no sync wave, no name label on the Job, no time limit, no retry limit, another hook, the label app.kubernetes.io/name, another volume, an envFrom, an init container, a value, another ConfigMap, a name of another service; then a copy with no Job whose Component still patches one.
then: Expects LoadBase to refuse each copy.
notes: ST-DLV-Q20, ST-DLV-REPO03.

title: The platform requirements and the reference name the owner Secret and mark the variables that only the migration Job reads
when: Writes the platform requirements and the reference of the components of ST-DLV-UC07-R06-T01.
then: Expects the secret need orders-database-owner with the key url, only STEGO_MIGRATION_URL and its _FILE form read by the mode migrate, and in the section Secrets of the reference one row for each variable with a secret source: STEGO_MIGRATION_URL from orders-database-owner and url, read by the migration Job only; DATABASE_URL and STEGO_CURSOR_KEY_FILE, read by the Deployment; and STEGO_SPICEDB_KEY_FILE, read by the Deployment and the migration Job.
notes: ST-DLV-Q20: names only, never a value.

title: The schema digest that names the migration Job is the same for the same schema and changes with a migration or the runtime
when: Takes the schema digest of a run of a source, a migration, the schema manifest and go.sum at a runtime pin; then of the same files in another order; of the run with a changed go.sum, a changed source and a new handler file; of the run with a new migration, a changed migration, a changed manifest, a tenancy migration and a renamed migration; and of the run at another runtime pin and with none.
then: Expects 64 lower-case hex digits; the same digest for the other order, the changed go.sum, the changed source and the new handler file; and another digest for each change of a migration or the manifest and for each other runtime pin.
notes: ST-DLV-Q20: a new apply cannot change the pod template of a Job, so a release that changes the schema gets a Job of a new name. stego deps, which writes go.sum, and a component fix that changes no schema keep the name (ST-BLD-UC01-R02-T01, ST-DIS-UC04-R01-T01).

title: The key files that the Job gets are the file settings that the migrate mode of the runtime reads, apart from its own
when: Parses the source of the service runtime in registry/runtime/service, follows each function of the package that ReadMigrationSettings calls, at any depth, and takes each constant whose value is a *_FILE variable that a call gets as an argument; then reads the variables with read_by_mode: migrate of each component of the registry.
then: Expects MigrationKeyFiles of delivery to be exactly the *_FILE variables that the migrate mode reads, less those that only the migrate mode reads, which the Job takes as its own.
notes: Drift guard of ST-DLV-Q20 (orchestrator, 2026-11-16): the runtime module does not import internal, so the test reads the runtime source. Mutations caught (2026-11-16): ReadMigrationSettings that also reads the cursor key file; an empty MigrationKeyFiles.

title: The migration Job of a browser-service takes the digest of its session schema, not of no file
when: schemaDigest runs with no runtime pin on the generated files of a browser-service: main.go, browser/schema.sql, browser/schema/schema.go and browser/handlers.go; then with the session table changed, with the schema package changed, and with main.go and the handlers changed.
then: Expects a digest other than the SHA-256 of no input; a new digest for each change of the session table or the schema package; and the same digest when only main.go and the handlers change.
notes: Walkthrough 7, B6: the Job of the browser-service portal was named portal-migrate-e3b0c44298, the digest of no file, in every release, because a browser-service has no migrations folder, no schema manifest and no runtime pin. Its mode migrate makes and checks the session table of browser/schema.sql with the package browser/schema, so those files are its schema.

title: The api mode and the background modes run in their own Deployments, each with its probes and the variables of its modes
when: Writes the base of the service orders of ST-DLV-TD02, in which the worker connection is read by the worker mode alone, with the modes api, worker and controller, builds it with plain kustomize with an overlay that sets the image and the Components secret-files and fs-group; then writes it with the modes api alone, worker and controller alone, and none; then for a service name of 57 characters; then reads it back with a worker Deployment of another name.
then: Expects the Deployments orders and orders-worker, the args --mode=api and --mode=worker --mode=controller, the readiness /readyz and /readyz/modes, the liveness /livez of each, the image of the overlay on each, no port on the worker, the worker credential in the worker Deployment alone (as a file with secret-files), no STEGO_MODE entry, the variables that every mode reads in each, no selector of the api Deployment or of the Service that takes a worker pod, and no worker credential in the migration Job; one Deployment for each one-side case with its readiness, the STEGO_MODE entry and the worker credential only with a worker mode; the long name refused; and the renamed worker Deployment refused by LoadBase.
notes: Level: service. The build uses the kustomize library, as plain kustomize does. Decided on ST-DLV-Q27 (W8-B4).

title: stego apply writes the Deployment of the api mode and that of the worker modes for a service of the runtime data path, and one Deployment for a browser-service

title: Fills scaffolded for a command, a query and a consuming worker compile against their contracts and build into the service
when: With the inventory project of the fifth walkthrough (testdata/walkthrough5) from stego init: stego fill create runs for the command place-order (command.command), the query open-orders (query.query) and the worker fulfill-orders, whose one trigger consumes (worker.worker); then stego test and stego fill sign of each fill with a key that the test run makes for the test only (ST-EXT-TD02), then stego validate, stego apply, stego deps, go build, go vet and go test of the fills, with no go mod tidy and no fill.yaml by hand. then: Each fill create writes fill.yaml, fill.go and fill_test.go; the service builds, and the test of each unfinished fill passes. The three later runs fail, the last one names the slot command.command, and the project does not change. Expects the manifest of each such fill to hold no collection key. Expects fill.go and fill_test.go of each fill to be in the package of the fill name with no hyphen: placeorder, openorders and fulfillorders.
notes: Finding G1 of the fifth walkthrough (2026-11-17): fill create knew only the slots of registry components, so it answered slot not found for the slots that validate asks for. A command or worker fill exports New and a query fill exports Fill, as the generated code that binds them calls. The run also proves B1 (a service whose only worker consumes) and B4 (stego deps once fills exist) on the user path. Walkthrough 7, B12: fill create wrote the package place_order; Go names a package in lower case with no underscore (follow-up worker, 2026-11-17).

title: A command and a worker declared after the first build get their contracts in a later apply

Validate passes with the fill that holds no code; apply writes the contract type LowStockScanFill and then fails with a fault that names workers[1].fill and low-stock-scan. Once the fill code is written, apply refuses low-stock-scan as untested; once it is qualified, apply changes nothing, and the service builds and the fill tests pass.

A fill of a command, query or worker that holds no Go code now builds nothing and is held to no fill rule, so generation goes on, and apply names the fill once it has written the contract.

Expects each run of stego test with the failing test to exit non-zero and to leave the manifest of place-order as it was. Expects stego test to record no evidence for place-order while its test imports a module that go.mod does not hold. Expects plan and apply to refuse the dot import, naming place-order, and plan to pass once it is gone. Expects the collection to be refused with a fault that names open-orders and says that a fill of the slot query.query names no collection.

title: The record names the service, the compiler, the registry and each component used with its version and digest

Expects no component of the active set to be missing and no other component to be listed.
notes: The active set of rest-crud holds six components, so a record that leaves out one component fails the test. The test finds the active set with the port resolver from the archetype, its default authentication and its bindings. The component digest is ST-GEN-DS01's; the test computes it with the same function, and ST-GEN-DS01-T01 proves that function. It runs the stego binary that the test builds once per run from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: A YAML parser alone reads every file and hash from the record

title: The record carries format version 6 and exactly the fields documented for it
when: With a project after stego apply: The test reads the record's fields. Then it writes the record back as format version 4 with the key data_path and runs stego apply again.
then: format_version is 6, every field is in the list for version 6, and every field apply always writes is present; after the second apply the record is of format version 6 again, with no data_path.
notes: Format version 2 adds service_name and makes the sha of each component its component digest (ST-GEN-DS01), where version 1 held the registry reference. Format version 3 adds archetype: the archetype's name and version and its runtime pin (ST-GEN-EN01, decision of 2026-11-10 under the Product owner's delegation, ST-GEN-Q04 (a)). Format version 4 added data_path, the data path of the run (ST-SUP-RC01-OC41), and format version 5 removes it, because the runtime data path is the only data path (ST-SUP-RC20-OC39; decided by orchestrator under owner delegation, 2026-11-12, single data path, RC20-OC39 PR 2). Format version 6 adds project_files, the digest of each generated file of the project folder out of the generated output, the platform requirements (ST-DLV-REPO01). This compiler reads versions 0 to 6 and drops the key data_path of a version 4 record (state.go). specs/state-format.md@9eca0564f7bb8cce12e7fc329fd3b47b940bb11c describes version 1. A change to a field breaks the test, so the change must update the list, and with it the format version.

It runs the stego binary that the test builds once per run from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

notes: Mutations caught: the declared issuer not read; a caller with no flow; a store actor beside a backing store need. Security review of PR #345, F1: the issuer is the first override value in the published model, so a user name, a password or a token put in the URL by mistake would be published. Mutations caught (agents/followups/fu-90/mut.log): the user info kept; the query and the fragment kept; a value with no scheme and host shown. Security review of PR #350: a password with an unencoded '/' (https://u:123/secret@host/realm) put the rest of the secret in the path, and the issuer took any scheme. Mutations caught (agents/followups/fu-94/mut.py, 2 of 2): any scheme accepted; a path with '@' shown. Security review of PR #362, low: the parse cuts the fragment and then the query before it reads the user info, so a '?' or a '#' in the user info put a part of it in the host (https://tok?en@host gave https://tok). The four probe cases of that review are in the table. Mutations caught (agents/fu-standing/mut-issuer.log): the raw '@' check removed; the %40 path check removed.

then: Expects one HTML file, with no src, href, srcset or other address whose value is not a data: address or a fragment of the same file; no link, img, iframe, object or embed element; and no @import, url() of another file, http or https address other than the SVG namespace, fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket or other call that can load from outside the file.

title: The view opens from its file address with no server, no network request and no error

then: Expects each view to render with its title and its diagram, table or empty-aspect card, no network request, and no error in the console.
notes: It runs a headless Chrome or Chromium that STEGO_BROWSER names, driven from Go over the DevTools protocol (the driver is in the same file; never Playwright, owner decision Q-G (1)), with every request that is not a file: or data: address failed and counted. title: Every view and the tour work under the content security policy of the view, with no violation

then: Expects the policy of the view to start with default-src 'none' and admit scripts only by sha256 hash and to end with require-trusted-types-for 'script', the viewer to run, and no violation, request or error; and the write of a text as HTML to be refused with a TypeError of trusted types.

Mutations caught: the viewer script hashed from another text; the first inline script not hashed (#342 F1). Mutations caught (agents/followups/fu-96/mut.py): the policy without trusted types; the viewer that writes a text as HTML (R02-T02 fails with the error).

then: Expects the interactive view to be hidden; six printed views, each with its title, its key and a page break after it; and each request flow as a numbered list with one item for each of its steps.
notes: It runs a headless Chrome or Chromium that STEGO_BROWSER names, driven from Go over the DevTools protocol (the driver is in the same file; never Playwright, owner decision Q-G (1)), with every request that is not a file: or data: address failed and counted. On the developer workstation it runs only when STEGO_BROWSER is set, so local checks stay small. On a CI runner it takes the runner's Chrome and never skips, so the proof run holds its result; the browser runs with no sandbox only on a GitHub-hosted runner (GITHUB_ACTIONS is true and RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT is github-hosted), and it dies with the test process.

title: The trust aspect shows each boundary, the tenancy and each default with its rule

then: Expects each boundary of the model, of the kinds network, verified identity, tenant scope, fill code and process; the tenancy kind and claim; each setting that comes from a default marked as a default with the rule that sets it; and no stated setting marked as a default.

then: Expects the map first with a region for each boundary, drawn at 0.78 of its size or more also with the details open, the access matrix next, the authorization points, what each operation checks and the grant paths folded and closed, and the details of the cell to say where the operation is decided.
notes: It runs a headless Chrome or Chromium that STEGO_BROWSER names, driven from Go over the DevTools protocol (the driver is in the same file; never Playwright, owner decision Q-G (1)), with every request that is not a file: or data: address failed and counted. On the developer workstation it runs only when STEGO_BROWSER is set, so local checks stay small. On a CI runner it takes the runner's Chrome and never skips, so the proof run holds its result; the browser runs with no sandbox only on a GitHub-hosted runner (GITHUB_ACTIONS is true and RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT is github-hosted), and it dies with the test process. Mutations caught: the tables not folded; the map drawn at the width of the column; no decision point in the details of a cell.

title: The model holds what each operation and command checks, traced to the declaration
when: Derives the model of a small service with the collection docs (create public, read, update) and the command archive.
then: Expects one check for each operation and the command, each with its resource type and permission or public, and the declaration path it comes from, such as entities[0].permissions.read or commands[0].permission.
notes: Mutation caught: the permission of a command not read.

title: The model holds the check of each ancestor in the path of a nested operation, the top one first: the decided parent of a list with its read permission, and each other ancestor with its existence and link only, traced to the declaration
when: Derives the model of a service whose docs of a folder are under the folders of a shelf: the shelves are a collection of their own, the read permission of the shelf and of the folder is view, and folder-docs serves read, update and list. Derives it again with no bound authorization, and checks models whose ancestor check names an entity that is not in it, whose decided ancestor grants name a role, whose check grants name a field, whose ancestor that is not decided names a permission, whose read marks an ancestor as decided, and whose decided parent of a list names no permission.
then: Expects folder-docs.update and folder-docs.read to check the shelf and then the folder with no permission, no grants, decided false and the rule ST-SUP-RC20-OC24, with the link field shelf_id and the scope entry of each. Expects folder-docs.list to check the shelf in the same way, and the folder as decided with folder#view from entities[1].permissions.read. Expects shelf-folders.list to have one decided ancestor and docs.read none, and the grant paths of folder#view in the model. Expects the authorization point of the update to name no ancestor read and to give the existence check, and that of the list to say that it first decides folder#view on the parent Folder. With no bound authorization, expects no ancestor permission: the decided parent has the rule ST-DECL-UC06-R01 and each other ancestor ST-SUP-RC20-OC24. Expects each changed model to be not valid.
notes: Walkthrough-3 and #333: the model did not show the parent chain check of nested routes (ST-SUP-RC20-OC24). The model and the handler take the chain from the one rule types.ParentChain. Mutations caught: the ancestors in the order parent first; the read permission of the operation's own entity used for the ancestor. Security review of PR #374, L1: the reference check now checks the kind of the element that grants, an entity and a link name. Security review of PR #383: the shelf had no resource type and no collection, which no generator builds (the rest-api generator refuses a parent that no collection exposes, and the entity of a collection with no resource type); the derivation now refuses an ancestor with no resource type (ST-GEN-UC08-R12-T03), so the fixture gives the shelf a collection and a read permission. ST-SUP-Q156 (b), 2026-11-17: only the parent of a list, a create or an upsert is decided; each other ancestor is checked for existence and its link only, with no permission.

title: The derivation and the generators refuse the same declarations: each planned entity with a resource type and a public read or no read permission, and each ancestor with no resource type
when: Takes the nested fixture of ST-GEN-UC08-R12-T02 and gives its entities to the entity planning of the command runtime (command.EntityFile, whose planEntity the rest-api, the command and the worker generators share) on each set that the generators plan: the entity of each collection and each entity with a resource type that a ref field of one names, and the entities that each command and each worker writes; and gives the fixture to the derivation. Then does the same with the read of the ancestor Folder public or not declared, the read of the collection entity Doc public, the read of Doc not declared with no bound authorization, a new entity Log with a resource type and no read named by a ref field of Doc, Log with the read public written by a command, Log with no read written by a worker, and Log with no read that nothing plans. Then gives the fixture and the fixture with no resource type on the ancestor Shelf to the rest-api generator and the second to the derivation.
then: Expects the generators and the derivation to accept the fixture and the unplanned Log, and both to refuse each other changed fixture: the generators name the public read or no read permission; the derivation gives an architecture refusal that names, for the ancestor, collections.folder-docs.scope, the entity Folder, entities[1], the resource type folder, the read, entities[1].permissions.read and ST-SUP-RC20-OC24, and otherwise the entity and its index, the read, what plans it (the collection, the ref field, the command or the worker), ST-SUP-RP10-LC13 and permissions.read as a permission of its resource type. Expects the rest-api generator to accept the fixture and to refuse the shelves with no resource type, and the derivation to refuse it, naming collections.shelf-folders.scope, the entity Shelf, entities[2] with no resource type, ST-SUP-RC20-OC24 and entities[2].resource_type.
notes: Security review of PR #374, L3: the model had branches for a public ancestor and for an ancestor with a resource type and no read permission, which no declaration that the generators build reached. The derivation now refuses them, so the model and the generators agree. Security review of PR #383, L2: planEntity refuses every planned entity with a resource type and a public or no read, also with no bound authorization and for an entity that is no ancestor, and the derivation refused only ancestors; it now refuses the same set. The branch of an ancestor with no resource type was not reached either, so the derivation refuses it too. Mutations caught: the derivation without the refusal of the ancestor (the model states a public ancestor check); the derivation without the refusal of the planned entities.

title: The derivation and the query runtime refuse the same declarations: each entity of the rest-api data path with a resource type and a public or no list permission
when: Takes the nested fixture of ST-GEN-UC08-R12-T02 and gives its entities to the read-only values of the query runtime (query.ViewFile, which the rest-api generator calls) on the entities of the rest-api data path: the entity of each collection and each entity with a resource type that a ref field of one names; and to the entity planning of the command runtime (command.EntityFile) on each set that the generators plan; and gives the fixture to the derivation. Then does the same with the list of the collection entity Doc public, the list of the collection entity Shelf not declared, the list of Doc not declared with no bound authorization, a new entity Log with a resource type, a read and no list named by a ref field of Doc, and Log written only by a command or only by a worker.
then: Expects the generators and the derivation to accept the fixture and Log written only by a command or a worker, and both to refuse each other changed fixture: the query runtime names its list permission; the derivation gives an architecture refusal that names the entity and its index, the public or no list permission, what plans it (the collection or the ref field), ST-SUP-RC33-OC01 and permissions.list as a permission of its resource type.
notes: From PR #384: query.ViewFile refused a planned entity with a resource type and a public or empty list permission, and the derivation did not, so the view could be built for a declaration that does not generate. Mutation caught: the derivation without the list check.

title: The derivation refuses a bound authorization with no compiled schema, an ancestor that the declaration does not state, and collections that a component other than rest-api serves
when: Derives the model of the fixture with a bound authorization and no compiled schema; of the nested fixture whose folder-docs scope names the entity Binder, which the declaration does not state, and gives that fixture to the rest-api generator too; of the fixture whose component that serves the collections is named other-api; and of the fixture with no component that serves the collections and no list permission on Doc.
then: Expects an architecture refusal that names the bound authorization, authz/schema.zed, the missing compiled schema and ST-GEN-UC08-R13; the rest-api generator to refuse the undeclared ancestor, and the derivation to refuse it, naming collections.folder-docs.scope, the entity Binder, that the declaration states no entity Binder, and ST-SUP-RC20-OC24; a refusal that names the component other-api that serves the collections and the component rest-api alone; and no refusal with no component that serves the collections.
notes: Security review of PR #384, L2: with a bound authorization and no schema, each permission was not complete but the role list said complete and empty, so the matrix said that no role is granted; the reconciler always gives the schema, so the derivation refuses the input. L3: the derivation said that an undeclared ancestor checks no permission, and planned the rest-api data path for any component that serves the collections; it now refuses both. The rest-api generator is the one generator of the collections. Mutations caught: the derivation without each refusal.

title: The grant paths are expanded from the schema with each arrow, userset, caveat, intersection, exclusion and wildcard, and each recursion stated
when: Derives the model with a schema in which doc#read is folder->view, folder#view is (viewer + parent->view) - banned, viewer admits user, user:* and group#member, group#member admits group#member, and doc#write is folder->edit + owner with folder#edit = editor & auditor and editor with the caveat ip_allowed.
then: Expects the paths of doc#read to be the viewer user, the viewer wildcard and the group member, each through the arrow and except folder#banned, and two paths that stop at a recursion with no role; and the paths of doc#write to be the owner direct, the auditor that requires the editor, and the editor under the caveat ip_allowed that requires the auditor. Expects the six roles.
notes: Mutations caught: the exclusion, the caveat, the wildcard or the intersection not stated; the recursion not detected.

title: The expansion of a wide and deep schema stops at a stated work limit, and the model says that its roles are not complete
when: Expands a schema of seven types in a chain, each of whose permission is the union of 40 arrows to the next type, once with a last permission that grants nothing and once with one that grants the owner; then derives the model of a command that checks it, and of the small service with its own schema.
then: Expects each expansion to stop within the bound of steps, with one last path that has no role: for the permission that grants nothing, of the kind work limit and not path limit, with a stop text that names the work limit; for the one that grants the owner, of the kind path limit and not work limit, with a stop text that starts with the path limit of 512 paths. Expects the cut permission and the role list of the model to say that they are not complete, and the role list of the small service to say that it is complete.
notes: Found by the security review of #341 (M1): the walk went on after the path cap and had no step bound, about 40^6 calls. The bound counts steps, not wall time. Security review of PR #388, L1: the path limit has its own kind. Mutations caught: the stop does not end the walk; a step bound 50 times higher; the role list not marked; the kind work limit for the path limit.

title: A caveat or an expiration on a relation, a userset or an arrow makes a conditional grant and its own role
when: Expands box#read = reader + viewer + team->member, where reader admits user and user with expiration, viewer admits team#member with in_hours, and the tupleset team admits team with in_hours.
then: Expects four paths: the reader user direct; the reader user with the kind expiration and its own role; the team member through the userset and through the arrow, each with the kind caveat and the caveat in_hours.
notes: Found by the security review of #341 (L2). Mutations caught: the caveat name not carried; the expiration not read; the caveat of the tupleset subject not carried through the arrow.

title: The expansion that reaches the path limit stops with one path of the kind path limit, whose stop text names that limit, and not the work limit
when: Derives the model of a service whose doc permissions read and write each pass one of 30 arrows to hub#mid, and hub#mid one of 30 arrows back to doc#read, so that each of the 900 paths is a recursion with no role. Then names the limit of a path of the kind path limit with no stop text.
then: Expects no role and the roles not complete; for doc#read and doc#write, not complete with 513 paths, no path of the kind work limit, and one path of the kind path limit with no role, whose stop text starts with the path limit of 512 paths and whose limit name is that text. notes: Security review of PR #388, L1: a path that the path limit stopped had the kind work limit, so the cell glyph and title said work limit while the note and the facts said the path limit of 512 paths. Mutation caught: the kind work limit for the path limit.

title: The access matrix has a line for each role and a cell for each operation, marked with the kind of grant, turned when the operations outnumber the roles

notes: Mutations caught: the matrix never turned; the operations not grouped by collection.

The test also needs at least one marked and one clear cell of a nested operation, so the fixture proves both. Mutation caught: the mark on every cell of a nested operation.

when: Renders the view of access.json, whose nested operations of org-users and org-settings read the organization first with organization#view, whose grant paths a limit cut short, and reads the head of each check, the cell of each role and the table of what each operation checks.

The owner uses the view for compliance questions. Mutation caught: the head with no mark for the ancestor read.
