Mutation caught: the details with no note for the ancestor read.

title: A cell of a role that no named path gives a permission whose grant paths a limit cut short says may hold, never no grant
when: Renders the view of access.json, whose organization#view a limit cut short, and reads the cell of each role and each check. Then renders it with the grant paths of organization#view complete, and with no key complete in member#view.
then: Expects each cell of a role that no path names, for a check whose permission is not complete, to be a button with the mark ⚠, the class may-hold, the title that says may hold, and the same text after the operation name as its screen reader label; and no such mark in another cell. The owner uses the view for compliance questions, so an incomplete grant set must never read as a definite no. Mutation caught: the cell that says no grant for an incomplete permission.

Security review of PR #383, L1 and L3: the details had no word for a role that may hold an incomplete permission, and the script read a permission with no key complete as complete. Mutation caught: the script that tests complete === false.

title: With no role that a grant path names, the access matrix says that no role is granted only when no limit cut a path short, and else shows the paths that stop

The owner uses the view for compliance questions. Mutation caught: the sentence for every matrix with no role.

title: With no role named, the note of the access matrix names the limit that stopped the grant paths, and a cell of the line of the paths that stop with no path of an incomplete permission says may hold

Then renders the model with no grant path of doc#write, as a reader can edit it, and then with no grant path of doc#read and doc#write.
then: Expects, for the derived model, no role, the roles not complete and one grant path of each permission that stops at the work limit and at no depth limit; the note no-role-named that no grant path reached a role before a limit stopped it, which names the work limit of 20000 steps and not the depth limit, and that the matrix does not say that no role holds one; no sentence that the schema grants no role; and in the line of the paths that stop a button for each check that is not public, which shows the work limit glyph and whose title names the work limit. Expects, with no path of doc#write, a note that names the work limit and a limit that the model does not name, no cell of the line of the paths that stop that says no grant, and each cell of a check of doc#write a button with the may hold glyph, the class may-hold, and the may hold text of the line of the paths that stop as its title and its label. notes: Security review of PR #385, L2: with no role named, the note said that the paths stopped before they reached a role, which does not name the cause, and in the line of the paths that stop a cell of an incomplete permission with no path that stops said no grant, a definite no for an incomplete set. The owner uses the view for compliance questions. Mutation caught: the cell no grant for the line of the paths that stop; the note with no limit named.

title: The trust view of a model whose grant paths the work limit stopped before a role names that limit, and a cell of the paths that stop with no path of an incomplete permission says may hold
when: A headless browser opens, at 1280 px and at 400 px, the trust and tenancy view of the model of ST-GEN-UC08-R14-T11 with no grant path of doc#write, and selects the cells of the paths that stop for docs.read and for docs.update.

title: A checkout by commit with no ref is not a repository with no commit
when: From ST-GEN-TD03 with its record: a branch change renames Note.title to heading with no schema change and removes .stego/state.yaml. Three new folders each run git init and git fetch of the branch change: the first with a full fetch and git checkout FETCH_HEAD, the second with --depth 1 and git checkout FETCH_HEAD, the third with --depth 1 and git checkout FETCH_HEAD -- . (HEAD not born, the repository shallow); stego plan and stego apply run in each with no --base. Six more new folders each run git init and a full fetch of change, which leaves HEAD not born, no ref and a repository that is not shallow: git checkout FETCH_HEAD -- .; git restore --source=FETCH_HEAD --worktree -- .; git read-tree -u --reset FETCH_HEAD; a fetch into main with no FETCH_HEAD, a checkout of main, an orphan branch and main deleted; git read-tree -u --reset FETCH_HEAD and FETCH_HEAD removed (only the object store holds commits); git read-tree -u --reset FETCH_HEAD and the object store emptied (only FETCH_HEAD exists); stego plan and stego apply run in each with no --base. Then, in a copy of the service whose branch main is renamed to trunk, an orphan branch with no record runs stego plan.
then: Expects each plan and apply to exit non-zero, to name the missing default branch, not to say that there is no base check, and to change no file; and plan on the orphan branch to exit non-zero and name the missing default branch.
notes: Finding H1 of the security review of PR 318: a repository is new only when HEAD names no commit, it has no ref, and it is not shallow. Medium finding of round 2 of that review: also only when the object store holds no commit and no FETCH_HEAD exists. Mutations caught (fu-73-mut3.py, 8 of 8): no FETCH_HEAD and no object check; no FETCH_HEAD check; no object store check; the object check on a wrong type; and, with the round-2 checks off, the old code (no ref is no commit), no HEAD check, no shallow check, no ref check.
